LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch as these two teams take center stage on "Thursday Night Football" after Week 7 losses IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect In the Week 8 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Green Bay Packers play host to the Carolina Panthers . The Packers enter this game off a disappointing loss to the division rival Detroit Lions , in a game they had multiple chances to win. Green Bay had won three in a row to salvage its season after a blowout loss to the Atlanta Falcons the last time the Packers played on Thursday night (Week 3), but they hit a bump in the road last week. Now, they're looking to make it four wins in five games. The Panthers are coming off an embarrassing blowout loss at the hands of the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Carolina was blasted 43-13 last week and was never truly competitive, falling down 17-0 early. However, the Panthers still sit at .500 after climbing that hump with their win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6. Now, they try to get back to their winning ways. Which of these two teams will get back in the win column? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Packers vs. Panthers live Date: Thursday, Oct. 29 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -3/5, O/U 47.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Panthers have the ball The Panthers limped to their worst offensive performance of the season last week, managing just 266 yards, 15 first downs and 13 points while turning the ball over four times. They had previously gained at least 340 yards in every game, gained at least 24 first downs in four of five, and scored 25-plus points in four of five. Bryce Young returned to poor form on Sunday, going only 14-of-27 for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while also fumbling once. He's now completed south of 52% of his passes in back-to-back games and south of 55% in three of his last four, with the only exception being a game against the decrepit Lions pass defense. Young got off to a hot start to the season , but he's cooled off a bit as of late. The Packers have been a tough matchup for opposing quarterbacks this year. They're eighth in net passing yards per attempt, and they've yet to allow more than 296 net passing yards in any game this season. They've also allowed just nine touchdown passes against nine interceptions. Jonathan Gannon has been good at limiting what opponents can do through the air, for the most part. It is, however, worth noting that the Packers faced Carson Wentz , Geno Smith , Michael Penix Jr. , Jalon Daniels and Tyson Bagent before getting Dak Prescott and Jared Goff over the last two weeks. So they haven't exactly done this against a murderer's row of opponents. Green Bay has gotten pressure at a below-average rate — no surprise with Micah Parsons still sidelined. Instead, the Packers have gotten by against the pass with sticky coverage and timely plays on the ball. Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse have been solid on the outside. Javon Bullard has played well in the slot, and the safeties are providing quality help over the top and in the middle of the field. Carolina's passing game is mostly built outside the numbers with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker , though Young has thrown over the middle more this season than in past years. It'll be up to the skyscrapers on the perimeter to win their one-on-one matchups here in order to give Young room to throw, though he should have more time than he did last week thanks to Green Bay's relatively weaker pass rush. In the run game, the Panthers lean on Chuba Hubbard , who is averaging 4.8 yards per carry in a workhorse role in the absence of Jonathon Brooks . Hubbard only got seven carries in the negative game script last week, but you can likely expect the Panthers to try to "Establish The Run" here as a way to get their offense back on track. Green Bay has allowed only 3.9 yards per carry this season, though, so it might be tough, especially with right tackle Taylor Moton now on the sidelines. When the Packers have the ball The Packers welcomed Josh Jacobs back to the lineup last week but still found themselves entirely unable to run the ball against the Lions. They totaled just 60 yards on the ground, with Jacobs himself carrying 11 times for only 36 yards. Green Bay is now averaging a pathetic 2.9 yards per carry on the season, which unsurprisingly ranks dead last in the league. The Panthers, meanwhile, were run over by the Bucs last week. Bucky Irving and Co. blew past Carolina for a remarkable 258 yards on the ground, which was made all the more incredible by the fact that the Panthers had yielded just 81 rushing yards in their previous two games combined. Still, Carolina has allowed 5.2 yards per carry on the season now, which, to no surprise, ranks dead last. Almost 60% of the rushing yards the Panthers have allowed, though, came in their games against the Bucs and the Chicago Bears in Week 1. They've been fine-ish against the run otherwise. So, can the Packers run the ball with any degree of success here? If the recent history of this season is any indication, then the answer is probably not. Jacobs has been at or below 4.0 yards per carry in two of his last three full seasons, and spending six weeks on the commissioner's exempt list in the wake of a disturbing domestic violence incident probably didn't make him a more efficient runner. And the offensive line is still not a good run-blocking unit. So, the fate of the Packers' offense likely once again falls on the right shoulder of Jordan Love . Love has only completed 59.8% of his passes at an average of 7.4 yards per attempt this season, but he's been victimized by a league-high 21 drops, according to Tru Media. Love is attacking deep downfield consistently, with a 9.1-yard average depth of throw that ranks fourth-highest in the NFL . As such, he's created explosive plays (16-plus-yard gains) at the third-highest rate in the league among 33 qualified quarterbacks. He should see favorable matchups when he looks downfield on Thursday night. Panthers starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson remain out on injured reserve, which has left rookie Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans as the starting corners. But Evans is also out on Thursday night, meaning, well, I honestly don't even know who is going to step up in his absence. The Panthers elevated Marco Wilson from the practice squad, and they may need to shift Chau Smith-Wade outside. Either way, it's not a great situation for Carolina. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , who is trending to play, should be able to find space down the field against these corners, and then it's just a matter of actually hanging onto the ball when Love puts it on them. Green Bay could have a big night through the air if the Packers can protect Love, which will be made easier by the absence of Panthers edge rusher Jaelan Phillips , who is also out for this game. It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Watson and Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better as of late after a rough start to the season. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. And as Dajani said, this Minnesota offense just does not have the ability to get into a high-scoring game and come away with a win. They need the defense to hold the opponent down entirely, and I'm not sure that even Flores' bunch can do that in the friendly confines of Ford Field. … Prediction: Lions 23, Vikings 14 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) Dajani (Steelers -3.5): How can the Browns keep getting away with this? They overcame a 14-0 deficit in Nashville on Sunday, as Harold Fannin Jr . took a short reception 36 yards down the field with 20 seconds remaining to set up a 32-yard game-winning field goal from Andre Szmyt . Deshaun Watson became the third quarterback since 1970 to register a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of the season. With this being a divisional game against an opponent that just got back from Paris, I can understand why some would take the points with the underdog given the hook. But the Steelers are 3-0 ATS at home. That includes Week 3, when they dropped 30 points on Joe Burrow and the Bengals in a win, and Week 5, when Pittsburgh scored 34 points in a double-digit victory over the Colts. The Steelers are averaging 26.0 points per game over their last five contests, which ranks top 10 in the NFL, and are 8-0 SU and ATS in their last eight home games vs. the Browns. In fact, Pittsburgh is actually a perfect 11-0 ATS in its last 11 home divisional games. Insane stat. … Prediction: Steelers 26, Browns 21 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): I don't understand how the Browns keep doing it. Every single one of their victories has required a game-winning drive in the final five minutes of the game. That's not sustainable on any level whatsoever. The Steelers don't exactly have consistency written all over them, considering the vagaries of their passing game and the fact that their three-game winning streak has come against weak opponents. However, I trust Jaylen Warren and Co. more than I do the Browns at this point. … Prediction: Steelers 20, Browns 13 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) Dajani (Falcons +2.5): I have plenty of questions about both of these teams, but I did tell you the Falcons were going to cover the small number vs. the 49ers last week! Atlanta finished that game on a 26-6 run after trailing 14-3. They scored on four straight drives. I'm not sure the Buccaneers deserve to be three-point favorites this week after that destruction of the Panthers. Baker Mayfield had to throw for just 64 yards and a touchdown in a 43-13 victory, as Bucky Irving , Kenneth Gainwell and Sean Tucker combined for 246 yards rushing and three touchdowns. This Falcons rush defense ranks fourth in the NFL with 88.9 rushing yards allowed per game. Plus, the Falcons have won two road games this season by 20+ points after being listed as an underdog, and are 4-0 ATS in their last four road games against the Buccaneers. … Prediction: Falcons 26, Buccaneers 24 Dubin (Falcons +2.5): The Buccaneers ran all over the Panthers last week, but Atlanta has actually been quite good against the run, allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season. Can Tampa really control the game with Bucky Irving the way it did last week, or will it have to actually turn Baker Mayfield loose as a passer here? If the Bucs have to do that, I have more confidence in Atlanta's offense right now, with Bijan Robinson , Drake London and even Kyle Pitts contributing at a high level. … Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 17 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Dajani ( Broncos +1.5): The Broncos had an embarrassing outing last time they played the Chiefs, allowing 247 yards off of 28 missed tackles in a 31-10 loss. There has been a lot of talk about Bo Nix and the offense, but what about the Chiefs? They averaged 4.3 yards per play and recorded just 213 yards of total offense in that embarrassing loss to the Seahawks. The team seemingly never got off the bus. It was the first game in Andy Reid's head-coaching career in which his team registered zero explosive plays,

Bryce Young, up until last week, had been playing leaps and bounds better than he had the previous three seasons, and I'm of the belief that it's more of a sign of an abnormally strong start against some bad defenses as opposed to a quarterback who improved by tenfold in a single offseason," he wrote. Sporting News' Bill Bender is taking the Packers, 27-22. "The Panthers have been wildly unpredictable this season, and it hinges on whether Bryce Young can bounce back from a bad outing against the Buccaneers. Green Bay has the worst rushing offense in the NFL (59.9 ypg). The Panthers have the worst rushing defense (153.3 ypg). Will Josh Jacobs get that running game on track?" he wrote. This means the Panthers are the ultimate underdogs here. Not only are they not favored, but no one's picking them to win. It's rare, but that does happen, even for a team that is probably solid like the Panthers. That could be where the Panthers operate best, as they usually win when they're not supposed to or are counted out. But after what we saw last week, it's not hard to see why they are universally being picked against. It couldn’t possibly go worse than when they lost to the Falcons 35-14 on Thursday night last month. “Yeah, I should change everything, huh?” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon sort-of joked on Wednesday, “because we laid an egg – me I’m talking about. I hold that to ourselves. I think Matt (LaFleur) made some tweaks, which I really liked. I think it’s going to help our guys. We’ll see, the proof will be in the pudding.” The Packers need to find a victory in the pudding against Carolina. Green Bay is in last place in the NFC North and holds a tenuous grip on the final spot in the NFC. Obviously, it’s early to be overly concerned about the playoff race, but the division race is in danger of getting away from them before the calendar flips to November. Will the Packers win? Here are our weekly predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Panthers Prediction The Packers and Panthers are two of the most beat-up teams in the NFL , a fact complicated by playing on a Thursday. The injuries are probably one reason why these also are among the most inconsistent teams in the league. It seems like the Packers have a lot of injuries. But is that true? Here's some good injury data shared by @RotoWire . ⬇️ https://t.co/Mp2IlrCeZW The Packers can’t get out of their own way on offense, which is why they’ve scored 20 or fewer points in four of seven games. They scored only 17 points last week against the Lions, who have one of the worst defenses in the NFL. Detroit entered the game on pace to blow away the dubious league record for passing yards allowed. Jordan Love and Co. failed miserably to capitalize, especially in key moments. The Panthers are no better. Remember Green Bay’s loss to Atlanta at Lambeau? That came just days after Carolina went into Atlanta and won by 31. The Panthers had won three of their last four games until getting steamrolled 43-13 by the Buccaneers. So, which team(s) will show up tonight? So, let’s bring it back to injuries. The Panthers’ starting cornerbacks, Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn, are on injured reserve. Their best pass rusher, Jaelan Phillips, will be inactive due to injury. So, there should be opportunities for the Packers to make plays in the passing game. Combined with a matchup against the worst run defense in the NFL, this could be a breakout game for Green Bay’s offense. “Should be,” of course, is the operative phrase. The only thing the Packers do consistently is play inconsistently. They can’t run the football. They struggle to protect the passer. They drop passes. They misfire on third down and squander opportunities in the red zone. So, should the Packers have a big game offensively? Yes. But will they? At least the defense is good, with Gannon earning his paycheck by fielding a formidable unit that has mostly played winning football even though it can’t rush the passer with a traditional four-man rush. So, who wins? I’d give the advantages to Green Bay on both sides of the ball. On offense, Love should have a strong game against Carolina’s depleted pass defense. Heck, they might even be able to run the football against the league’s worst rush defense. On defense, the Packers have spoken highly of Panthers quarterback Bryce Young all week, but Young is not as good as Detroit’s Jared Goff and the Panthers have only one big-time threat in the passing game compared to two for Detroit. The Panthers will be without their preferred starting offensive tackles, too. So, the Packers will score a key win. A 5-3 start with Micah Parsons still not back on the practice field would be a major victory for a team that has aspirations to be playing deep into January. Bill’s Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 17. Bill’s Record: 5-2. The injuries on the offensive line make for some uncertainty, and give this coaching staff a chance to screw up the starting five combination, like they have so many times in the past. That being said, Carolina is missing some big guns on defense, including their star pass rusher. Even if Matthew Golden cannot go or is on limited reps, Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft should be able to make enough plays in the passing game. Perhaps Josh Jacobs can finally find some room to roam on the ground against the league's worst run defense. Expect a sloppy game, but the Packers will make one more play than the Panthers, getting them to 5-3 before a much-needed mini bye week. Jacob’s Prediction: Packers 17, Panthers 14. Green Bay is set as a 3.5-point favorite at home in this primetime matchup, and it’s looking to stay over .500 in the 2026 season after a Week 7 loss to Detroit. Despite a three-game winning streak earlier this season and a 4-3 record overall, the Packers are in last place in the NFC North heading into Week 8. So, every game means a ton for Jordan Love, Matt LaFleur and Co. as they look to get back to the playoffs. Bryce Young and the Panthers are in a different spot, as they’re in first place in the weak NFC South despite going 3-3 through their first six games. Carolina lost at home to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 7, and it only has a half-game lead over the Atlanta Falcons in the division. The Panthers won the NFC South last season, but a litany of injuries to open the 2026 campaign have put them in a tough spot to repeat. Still, oddsmakers aren’t expecting them to have another blowout loss with this spread set inside a touchdown on Thursday. All week long, the SI Betting team has shared our favorite game picks, props, anytime touchdown scorer selections and more for Panthers vs. Packers. Here’s a quick look at some of our favorites to give our readers a one-stop shop to prepare for Thursday Night Football. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Panthers vs. Packers Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Green Bay Packers -3.5 (-110) vs. Carolina Panthers – Iain MacMillan Josh Jacobs Anytime TD (-145) – Peter Dewey Bryce Young OVER 1.5 Touchdown Passes (-111) – Peter Dewey Matthew Golden OVER 4.5 Receptions (-139) – Peter Dewey Earlier this week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite bet for every NFL game in his Road to 272 column , and he’s taking the Packers to win and cover on Thursday: I wrote about how I was out on the Panthers last week, and I proved to be right as they ended up on the wrong side of a blowout against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. I'm still out on this Panthers team, as they seem like a significant regression candidate after a strong start to the season. Bryce Young, up until last week, had been playing leaps and bounds better than he had the previous three seasons, and I'm of the belief that it's more of a sign of an abnormally strong start against some bad defenses as opposed to a quarterback who improved by tenfold in a single offseason. The Packers' defense ranks 12th in opponent EPA per play and 10th in opponent EPA per dropback, so with them being on their home field on a short week, I expect them to get to Young in this game. I'll take the Packers to cover on Thursday Night Football. Packers running back Josh Jacobs missed the first six weeks of the season on the Commissioner's Exempt List, but he returned in Week 7 and made an immediate impact against the Detroit Lions. Jacobs played just 52.2 percent of Green Bay’s offense snaps, but he saw 18 opportunities (11 rushes, seven targets) and ended up finding the end zone. The former first-round pick had 11 carries for 36 yards and caught five of his seven targets for 55 yards (and a receiving score) in the loss to Detroit. He has a great matchup against a Carolina defense that is 30th in EPA/Rush, 32nd in yards per carry allowed and 32nd in rushing touchdowns allowed (11) this season. While this isn’t the most favorable price, Jacobs has been a touchdown machine in his Packers career, scoring 31 times in 33 games. He’s an easy bet against one of the worst run defenses in the NFL. Bryce Young has been one of the best passers in the NFL even with his rough showing in Week 7 against Tampa Bay. In six games, Young has thrown for 1,712 yards and 12 scores, reaching at least 281 passing yards in five of his six games. He’s also posted four games with multiple touchdown passes. Green Bay is fifth in the NFL in EPA/Pass, but the Lions showed in Week 7 that you can throw on this team by attacking the outside corners. They lined Amon-Ra St. Brown – usually their slot receiver – outside quite a bit, and he finished the day 153 receiving yards. Plus, deep-ball threat Jameson Williams had two scores and 91 yards in the win. So, I expect Young and the Panthers to air it out against Green Bay, which has still allowed nine passing scores this season. Young has 36 or more pass attempts in five of his six games, so I think he’s a strong bounce-back candidate after a weird Week 7 game got out of hand very quickly for Carolina. Love has thrown the ball quite a bit in the 2026 season, and former first-round pick Matthew Golden has been one of the biggest beneficiaries. Through seven games, Golden has 69 targets, 36 catches and 540 receiving yards. He’s also found the end zone three times. Now, Love and Golden haven’t connected as much as you’d expect given his target share, but the second-year wideout still has five games with at least five receptions. Golden also has six or more targets in every game and four games with 12 or more looks. So, the volume should be there against a Carolina defense that is pretty average against the pass (13th in EPA/Pass) this season. I think Golden is undervalued at this number in Week 8. The Ravens acquired wide receiver Diontae Johnson and a sixth-round pick in 2025 on Tuesday from the Carolina Panthers for a 2025 fifth-rounder. The Panthers announced the terms of the trade late Tuesday. Johnson had been Carolina’s leading wide receiver since being acquired in an offseason trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers for cornerback Donte Jackson. Johnson has 30 receptions for 357 yards and three touchdowns for Carolina, but did not play in Sunday’s 28-14 loss to the Denver Broncos because of a rib injury. Johnson was set to become an unrestricted free agent after the season. According to a person familiar with the trade, two other teams expressed interest in acquiring Johnson before the Ravens got involved a couple of days ago. Given the compensation for Johnson, it’s likely that some teams were scared off by his past issues in the locker room. Eager to improve their draft positioning for next season, the Panthers are likely to listen to more calls before the Nov. 5 trade deadline. Johnson joins second-year wide receiver Zay Flowers and 24-year-old Rashod Bateman — plus a handful of capable tight ends — among Jackson’s options. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. And as Dajani said, this Minnesota offense just does not have the ability to get into a high-scoring game and come away with a win. They need the defense to hold the opponent down entirely, and I'm not sure that even Flores' bunch can do that in the friendly confines of Ford Field. … Prediction: Lions 23, Vikings 14 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) Dajani (Steelers -3.5): How can the Browns keep getting away with this? They overcame a 14-0 deficit in Nashville on Sunday, as Harold Fannin Jr . took a short reception 36 yards down the field with 20 seconds remaining to set up a 32-yard game-winning field goal from Andre Szmyt . Deshaun Watson became the third quarterback since 1970 to register a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of the season. With this being a divisional game against an opponent that just got back from Paris, I can understand why some would take the points with the underdog given the hook. But the Steelers are 3-0 ATS at home. That includes Week 3, when they dropped 30 points on Joe Burrow and the Bengals in a win, and Week 5, when Pittsburgh scored 34 points in a double-digit victory over the Colts. The Steelers are averaging 26.0 points per game over their last five contests, which ranks top 10 in the NFL, and are 8-0 SU and ATS in their last eight home games vs. the Browns. In fact, Pittsburgh is actually a perfect 11-0 ATS in its last 11 home divisional games. Insane stat. … Prediction: Steelers 26, Browns 21 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): I don't understand how the Browns keep doing it. Every single one of their victories has required a game-winning drive in the final five minutes of the game. That's not sustainable on any level whatsoever. The Steelers don't exactly have consistency written all over them, considering the vagaries of their passing game and the fact that their three-game winning streak has come against weak opponents. However, I trust Jaylen Warren and Co. more than I do the Browns at this point. … Prediction: Steelers 20, Browns 13 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) Dajani (Falcons +2.5): I have plenty of questions about both of these teams, but I did tell you the Falcons were going to cover the small number vs. the 49ers last week! Atlanta finished that game on a 26-6 run after trailing 14-3. They scored on four straight drives. I'm not sure the Buccaneers deserve to be three-point favorites this week after that destruction of the Panthers. Baker Mayfield had to throw for just 64 yards and a touchdown in a 43-13 victory, as Bucky Irving , Kenneth Gainwell and Sean Tucker combined for 246 yards rushing and three touchdowns. This Falcons rush defense ranks fourth in the NFL with 88.9 rushing yards allowed per game. Plus, the Falcons have won two road games this season by 20+ points after being listed as an underdog, and are 4-0 ATS in their last four road games against the Buccaneers. … Prediction: Falcons 26, Buccaneers 24 Dubin (Falcons +2.5): The Buccaneers ran all over the Panthers last week, but Atlanta has actually been quite good against the run, allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season. Can Tampa really control the game with Bucky Irving the way it did last week, or will it have to actually turn Baker Mayfield loose as a passer here? If the Bucs have to do that, I have more confidence in Atlanta's offense right now, with Bijan Robinson , Drake London and even Kyle Pitts contributing at a high level. … Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 17 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Dajani ( Broncos +1.5): The Broncos had an embarrassing outing last time they played the Chiefs, allowing 247 yards off of 28 missed tackles in a 31-10 loss. There has been a lot of talk about Bo Nix and the offense, but what about the Chiefs? They averaged 4.3 yards per play and recorded just 213 yards of total offense in that embarrassing loss to the Seahawks. The team seemingly never got off the bus. It was the first game in Andy Reid's head-coaching career in which his team registered zero explosive plays,

There are a ton of great division races shaping up, and some of those headline a Week 8 slate with a ton with playoff implications. The Baltimore Ravens are hoping to get Lamar Jackson back for a matchup with Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills, though the odds in that game show that the Bills have an edge after Baltimore lost a second straight game without the two-time MVP on Sunday. Baltimore isn't the only AFC North team facing a critical Week 8 game, as the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns -- the top-two teams in the division -- face off for the second and final time in 2026 with the winner set to start the season at 6-2. Who would've predicted that before Week 1? In the AFC West, the top two teams -- Denver and Kansas City -- play for the final time in the regular season after Kansas City dominated Bo Nix and Co. in the season opener. A win would put Denver back in the conversation to repeat as the division champions, but oddsmakers have set Kansas City as a road favorite in that game. In the NFC, the Chicago Bears and Seattle Seahawks play a huge matchup for the playoff picture on Monday night. Chicago is coming off a massive primetime win over New England and has not lost a game that Caleb Williams has started and finished in 2026. Each week, the SI Betting team breaks down the opening lines for the NFL games, as it’s important to see how the lines shift throughout the week before placing any bets. Plus, the opening odds can tell us just how important an injury, a recent loss or a rest disadvantage impacts the spread. There are four teams on the bye in Week 8: the San Francisco 49ers, New Orleans Saints, New York Giants and Houston Texans. That means there are 14 games once again, with the Green Bay Packers and Carolina Panthers opening things up on Thursday night. Lamar Jackson is back for Baltimore, giving football fans just the treat we wanted: a showdown with Buffalo QB Josh Allen. My Ravens vs. Bills predictions lean into that QB competition and what could be the most fun game on Sunday's slate. Here are my best NFL picks for this AFC heavyweight bout on Nov. 1. TOP Pick Ravens vs Bills prediction: Bills moneyline The return of Lamar Jackson has understandably dragged down the market on the Buffalo Bills . That offers a better ask on the home team's moneyline. The former MVP comes back from an ankle injury just in time, as this offense was getting stale under backup QB Tyler Huntley . But Jackson isn't 100% and his mobility will be tested early by the Bills defense, with the 11th-highest pressure rate per dropback. Baltimore's offensive line might not be up to the challenge, with injuries stacking up. Making plays with his legs has been a huge part of Lamar's success in recent meetings with Buffalo, rushing for 54, 70, and 73 yards in their three most recent matchups. Buffalo has had two weeks to rest and prep for Jackson and the Ravens , coming off a Week 7 bye. That also allows the Bills to get difference makers back on both sides of the ball, including WR1 D.J. Moore and DE Ed Oliver . Not only is Buffalo holding the rest edge, but this is its first home game in new Highmark Stadium in nearly a month. The last time the Bills were in front of the Mafia faithful, they were upset by the rival Patriots in Week 4. A win over Baltimore puts Buffalo back in the driver's seat of the AFC. Ravens vs Bills combo I'm siding with the Bills to pick up the win at home, leaning on Josh Allen to come through like he always does and for this Buffalo pass rush to make Jackson feel uncomfortable under center. Allen's nose for the end zone is incredible, and he's scored four total touchdowns in his last two meetings with the Ravens. On top of that, he always uses his legs in the biggest games, averaging more than 43 rushing yards in his last 14 contests with spreads in the four-point range. Allen already has eight rushing touchdowns in six games this year and rumbled for 14 last year, including two touchdowns against the Ravens in their Week 1 shootout. The edge rusher has six sacks and 39 pressures, second among edge defenders, according to PFF . On Sunday at New Highmark Stadium, he could be chasing Lamar Jackson. Jackson practiced fully Wednesday and Thursday, his first full sessions since a high ankle sprain knocked him out of the Week 4 win over Tennessee, per the Ravens . Head coach Jesse Minter laid out the standard Monday. "If he's able to play, healthy enough to play the way we feel like he needs to play, then he will play," Minter said, per the team's website . Buffalo (5-1) comes out of its bye with two straight wins, the latest a 33-30 decision in Las Vegas. Baltimore (4-3) has lost two straight and led Cincinnati 13-0 at halftime last week before giving up 35 unanswered points in a 35-13 loss. The Bills are a 3-point favorite , and here are four bold predictions for Sunday. Greg Rousseau sacks Lamar Jackson twice Oct 12, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Buffalo Bills linebacker Greg Rousseau (15) blocks a field goal from Los Angeles Rams place kicker Harrison Mevis (92) during overtime at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Rousseau's 85.5 pass-rush grade ranks fifth among 112 edge defenders, and he has 16 quarterback hits and three forced fumbles. He's carried a group that has 11 sacks as a team, per NFL.com , with Bradley Chubb at 1.5 and T.J. Parker pulling snaps away from Chubb . Chubb and Parker were both limited in practice this week. Baltimore's line is banged up. Rookie guard Vega Ioane returned to practice as a limited participant Thursday after a knee sprain that cost the Ravens a key piece of their offensive line, and John Simpson was limited Wednesday with a groin injury. A quarterback coming off a high ankle sprain may not escape the way he usually does. Bold prediction: Rousseau gets Jackson on the ground twice. Josh Allen runs for two touchdowns Oct 18, 2026; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) breaks a tackle and throws a touchdown pass in the third quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium.David Brytus-Imagn Images Josh Allen has 240 rushing yards and eight rushing touchdowns, two more scores on the ground than James Cook. His arm hasn't been as sharp. Allen's 70.4 passing grade ranks 18th, and his 11 turnover-worthy plays rank 26th of 35 quarterbacks, according to PFF . The Ravens know what's coming. "We know that he's a bigger body, and we know that he's fast as well and he can scramble out well to his right," outside linebacker Mike Green said, per the Ravens' website . Baltimore's defense ranks 18th in EPA per play, according to Sumer Sports , and linebacker Roquan Smith and safety Kyle Hamilton both missed Wednesday's practice with knee injuries before returning Thursday. Bold prediction: Allen runs for two touchdowns, giving him 10 on the season. Zay Flowers is held under 60 yards Oct 18, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers (4) runs through the tackle of Cleveland Browns linebacker Carson Schwesinger (49) in the second quarter at Huntington Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Scott Galvin-Imagn Images This is the boldest of the four. Zay Flowers has 40 catches for 608 yards, and his 90.6 grade ranks fourth among receivers, according to PFF . He had eight catches for 137 yards against the Bengals, including a 48-yard touchdown on a screen. Buffalo's defense ranks last in EPA per play allowed, per Sumer Sports , and leads the league with 12 defensive holding penalties. "We're not a very good defense at overcoming adversity in the form of penalties right now," defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard said, per the Bills' website . C.J. Gardner-Johnson is suspended for this game, so Damar Hamlin is expected to start at safety next to Cole Bishop. Cornerback Maxwell Hairston's 36.4 coverage grade ranked 98th of 102 corners when we looked at the pass defense during the bye, so Flowers will have chances. Davison Igbinosun's seven passes defensed lead the team. Bold prediction: Leonhard's group keeps Flowers under 60 yards. D.J. Especially after last week’s blown two-score lead to the Cleveland Browns, nobody is expecting Robert Saleh’s first team in Nashville to execute a miraculous turnaround. Draft discussions are already becoming relevant, if that tells you anything. Still, the Titans hit the road to face the Cincinnati Bengals this coming Sunday, and it’s a chance for Tennessee to win their second game in three weeks. That’s somehow still an exciting prospect. To preview the matchup, I’ve got one reason the Titans will beat the Bengals, one reason they won’t, and my own prediction for what will actually happen. Let’s start with the former. Will: Titans’ secondary sees massive uptick Two weeks in a row now, Tennessee has forced at least one interception. The Titans have come down with three picks over the last two games, two of which belong to rising offseason pickup Cor’Dale Flott. Tennessee Titans cornerback Cor'dale Flott (18) intercepts Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) on Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. Tennessee is facing one of the best pass-first teams in the NFL. If Saleh's secondary can find consistency beyond the occasional turnover, the Titans would have more than a fair chance to shut down RB Chase Brown on the ground, too. It's much easier to stop Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins in concept than it is on the field, but doing so is the Titans' key to winning this one. Won’t: Titans can't overcome inconsistent Bengals defense The inverse, of course, is if the Titans' offense continues to suffer. The Bengals have proved themselves beatable against "bad" teams - just see their narrow, one-score win over the 1-6 Miami Dolphins two weeks ago. But Cincinnati also just dismantled the Baltimore Ravens last week, 35-13. The through line is that Cincy scored 30+ points in both of those contests; it comes down to the opposing offense's ability to hang in there when Burrow and his crew get hot. Tennessee ranks 31st in both touchdowns and points per game. Almost everywhere the Bengals are in the top 10 through the air, the Titans are in the bottom 10. Cincy has allowed 20+ points in four of their six games this season. If Cam Ward can get back on his feet in any sense of the saying, another 24-point performance like Tennessee had last week could be enough to at least make this one interesting. However, the Titans may need a little more juice than they've seen yet this season from their QB to stay in it. Prediction: Titans lose, 31-20 Ultimately, I have the Titans falling to 1-7 in this one. We've seen a number of trends solidify that this roster has failed to prove their ability to rise beyond. Carnell Tate is the primary receiver in an otherwise underwhelming offense. The defense can force early turnovers, but can't get late stops when it matters - especially when it comes to tackling. Ward has a better second half than his typically abysmal first, but by the time Tennessee tries to get aggressive, it's too late to make a difference. I expect most of, if not all of these notes to be hit in Week 8. I don't think the Titans will lose in a blowout, but on the road against one of the best offenses in the league, this one already looks like too much for Saleh's team. picks.headline: Titans scouting report vs Cincinnati Bengals, matchups, prediction NFL Week 8
picks.blurb: News Sports Counties Business Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals TITANS Titans scouting report vs Cincinnati Bengals, matchups, prediction NFL Week 8 Tyler Palmateer Nashville Tennessean Oct. 28, 2026, 5:04 a.m. CT The Tennessee Titans will face the Cincinnati Bengals in NFL Week 8 following a 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns. The Bengals' passing offense, led by quarterback Joe Burrow, poses a significant challenge to the Titans' struggling defense. Positives are hard to find amid the Tennessee Titans’ struggles, but running back Tony Pollard was one last week. The Memphis native had his second-best game as a Titans player, with 129 yards rushing and three touchdowns on 25 carries in a gutting 27-24 home loss to the Cleveland Browns on Oct. 25. Maybe Pollard can do it again when the Titans (1-6) face the Cincinnati Bengals (4-2) at Paycor Stadium on Nov. 1 (noon CT, CBS) in NFL Week 8. The Bengals' and Browns ' run defenses are about the same statistically. Cincinnati allows 116.3 rushing yards per game, which ranks 19th in the league. The Titans gained a season-high 322 yards of offense with Pollard’s contributions, taking pressure off developing second-year quarterback Cam Ward . Tennessee coach Robert Saleh pinned the Browns loss on defense . Now that unit will face Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow, who’s 11th in the league with 1,653 yards passing, and second with 15 passing touchdowns, to go with three interceptions. Here’s our scouting report for the Titans’ game against the Browns. One Cincinnati Bengals stat to know Cincinnati has 13 pass plays of 25 yards or more this season. Tennessee has seven. Where Tennessee Titans have edge vs. Bengals The good news: Cincinnati’s offense ranks 29th in rushing yards per game (81.2), so there’s an opportunity for the Titans to make the Bengals one-dimensional. The bad news: Cincinnati’s offense is doing fine without a rushing threat, averaging 345.2 yards. It isn’t a big Titans advantage, but they must capitalize on it and see if stopping the run allows their pass rush to play like it did against the Colts (six sacks). It will take a stark turnaround after Tennessee allowed a season-high 183 yards rushing against the Browns. That marked the franchise’s worst single-game Pro Football Focus run defense grade (36.3) since 2023. Personnel changes up front have not helped. Run-stopping defensive tackle Jordan Elliott was released on Oct. 20 after breaking the NFL's gun policy . Third-year defender Timmy Horne was signed from the practice squad to replace him. Where Cincinnati Bengals have edge vs. Titans Tennessee’s secondary tackled poorly and took bad angles against the Browns, making rookie receiver KC Concepcion look like a Pro Bowler (eight catches, 129 yards). Imagine what Burrow and receivers Tee Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase might do. The Titans haven't seen an offense like this in 2026. The Bengals are seventh in the league in passing yards per game (264) and get 76% of their total yards through the air. Higgins and Chase have accounted for nine of the Bengals’ 13 explosive pass plays. Saleh’s also soul-searching in his secondary. Alontae Taylor was signed in the offseason to fortify one of Tennessee’s outside corner spots, but he was made inactive in Week 6 by coach’s decision and didn’t see the field in Week 7. Now it looks like Taylor will likely move to nickel . This would be a good week for Taylor to make a contribution, assuming Saleh plays him. Score prediction: Bengals 35, Titans 21 The Titans' scarred defense won’t be able to slow Burrow, and they can’t depend on Ward to keep pace in a shootout. It looks like their worst-case scenario matchup. Winning the turnover battle and making a few plays on special teams would help, but the Titans will be fortunate to keep it within 14 points. Tyler Palmateer covers the Tennessee Titans for The Tennessean. Have a story idea for Tyler? Reach him at tpalmateer@tennessean.com and on the X platform, @tpalmateer83 .

home.headline: Zac Taylor provides final injury update ahead of Bengals vs. Titans
home.blurb: Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said All-Pro wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase is ready to go for the upcoming game against the Tennessee Titans (1-6) on Nov. 1 at Paycor Stadium. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. Cincinnati placed tight end Erick All on injured reserve this week after he tore his ACL for the third time in his career. The position the Bengals are most thin at heading into Sunday's game is tight end with All now sidelined. Tanner Hudson was placed on injured reserve a week prior, and so the Bengals will rely on rookie seventh-round pick Jack Endries to back up Drew Sample and Mike Gesicki. But after snapping a two-game skid on Monday night, the Dallas Cowboys are chomping at the bit to get back on the field. My Cardinals vs. Cowboys predictions like Dallas to ride the momentum of that MNF victory, especially the reawakening of this explosive offense. Here are my best NFL picks for Nov. 1. TOP Pick Cardinals vs Cowboys prediction: Cowboys -6.5 The Dallas Cowboys broke out of a two-game funk in which the offense stalled out on third downs. Against Philadelphia, the Cowboys finished 9-for-14 on third/fourth downs and reclaimed their spot among the Top 5 attacks in Week 7. The Arizona Cardinals defense has been at the mercy of a very tough schedule, and it shows in its ratings (28th in EPA/play). While the offense was able to counter their opponents' scores earlier in the year, Arizona's attack is sputtering with the third-lowest points per play average over the last three contests. Dallas is more than happy turning this game into a track meet and thrives on the clean indoor surface at AT&T Stadium. Dak Prescott especially enjoys Jerry's World, with his career metrics spiking at home (103.4 rating at home vs. 92.8 on road). This is Dallas first "normal" home game since Week 2 (played TNF at home in Week 5), and I'm grabbing this Cowboys offense short of the key number of a touchdown. Cardinals vs Cowboys combo Arizona was in a similar shootout spot with Detroit a few weeks back and couldn't keep pace with an explosive offense. Dallas does the same here, pulling away with plenty of points in the second half. CeeDee Lamb is coming off a two-TD day in Week 7 and faces a Cardinals defense allowing the second most touchdowns to rival receivers. Michael Wilson needs to be more involved, and Mike LaFleur knows it. With Arizona playing from behind, plenty of passes come his way, and projections call for as many as 70 yards on Sunday. CeeDee Lamb touchdown Michael Wilson 60+ receiving yards Cardinals vs Cowboys touchdown scorer: CeeDee Lamb CeeDee Lamb looks like the best receiver in the NFL and is coming off a huge performance on Monday, catching two touchdown passes to give him six scores on the season. Lamb will rip through an Arizona secondary ranked among the worst in the land but also featuring plenty of bodies on the injury report in Week 8. The Cardinals run one of the highest rates of zone coverage, and Lamb is excellent at spotting seams in that defense. He's not only a downfield threat but also a catch-and-run weapon, exploiting an Arizona stop unit giving up the seventh most yards after the catch. The Cardinals have allowed 10 touchdowns to WRs (second most), and Lamb's TD forecasts for Week 8 all sit at 60% or higher, with some projections at 80%. away.headline: Arizona Cardinals' Jeremiyah Love to make his return in Week 8
away.blurb: Arizona Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love returned to the practice field as a limited participant on Wednesday and Thursday after missing the last two games with a lingering ankle injury. Jeremiyah Love to make his return "Even though he's been out for two weeks, none of these guys are 100 percent," Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFluer said via Bo Brack, Arizona Cardinals reporter and host of the PHNX Cardinals Podcast. "He's feeling as good as he can feel; we'll go from there." Christian Watson details gritty return to Packers' 'TNF' win over Panthers after breaking rib, spitting up blood In five games this season, Love has rushed 67 times for 245 yards and one touchdown, adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and another score. Love was averaging 16.2 opportunities per game before being sidelined with the ankle injury. Love suffered a right high ankle sprain during the preseason on Aug. 13, during his debut against the Las Vegas Raiders. In Love's absence, the Cardinals have used a running back-by-committee approach with Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight. The backfield remained a near-even timeshare, with Knight continuing to show higher rushing efficiency while Allgeier matched him in receptions and receiving yards. Knight began to make a compelling case for a larger share of Arizona's backfield workload. Against the Rams in Week 6, he turned 15 carries into 80 yards, averaging an efficient 5.3 yards per attempt, while Allgeier managed just 38 yards on 18 carries. The trend continued in Week 7, as Knight generated 48 yards on only seven rushes compared to Allgeier's 19 yards on eight attempts, though Allgeier provided added value as a receiver with three catches for 30 yards. Arizona's rushing attack isn't overwhelming opponents with sheer talent. It's doing it with design, discipline, and deception. The Cardinals rank among the NFL's top 15 rushing offenses in both EPA per play and success rate, consistently using pulling linemen, multiple tight-end sets, and pre-snap motion to force defenders into hesitation and create favorable running lanes. The Cowboys' Cardinals problem isn't going away The Cardinals will play the Dallas Cowboys , an NFL franchise they've found a lot of success against recently, winning their last four matchups, and eight of the last nine, according to Ed Werder, Dallas Cowboys insider for WFAA. "The Cardinals (4) currently join Dallas' NFC East rivals Philadelphia (7), New York (5) and Washington (5) as the only teams with 4+ road wins at AT&T Stadium," Werder wrote on Oct. 27 . "Arizona's 4-game winning streak at AT&T Stadium is its longest winning streak at any road venue." Want more articles like this? Follow Yardbarker on MSN to see more of our exclusive NFL content. away.headline: Arizona Cardinals reveal Jeremiyah Love status, role vs. Cowboys
away.blurb: LaFleur was asked whether Love will be back to 100%, now that he is cleared to return to game action. “You say 100% — even though he's been out for two weeks, none of these guys, by Nov. 1 are truly at 100,” LaFleur said. “He's feeling as good as he can feel. So kinda go from there.” “We're never gonna put a guy out there that we don't think can obviously benefit the team, benefit the offense,” LaFleur said. “… He's out there for a reason and we expect him to go.” Given that Love was limited by his ankle injury over the next two weeks — and that the Cardinals shut him down to get him close to 100% — it seems likely that they want to get him close to that workload, at least as it pertains to snap share. Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said that the rookie running back “will be good” to go against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8. Love had missed the Cardinals two previous games with a lingering injury to his left ankle. The injury first surfaced earlier in the season, as Love attempted to play through the issue. But after an ineffective performance against the Detroit Lions in Week 5, the Cardinals decided to shut him down so that he could regain his full explosiveness. LaFleur was later asked whether that means that Love will have access to his full complement of plays, or if there will be limitations to his role. As such, the expectation appears to be that Love will regain his full workload as the Cardinals’ starting running back, with Tyler Allgeier as the backup and Bam Knight as the third-string option. In four of his five games this season, Love has played fewer than 50% of snaps, with Allgeier seeing more work in three of those contests. However, the most notable comparison point may have come in Week 3, against the San Francisco 49ers. In that game, Love played 64% of snaps, took 21 of 23 carries and ran a route on 38.9% of dropbacks. Each of those were season highs. LaFleur also explained last week that he views Allgeier as more of a third down back, as the Cardinals’ most effective option in pass protection and in short-yardage situations. That would open Love up to a larger role on early downs, including as a pass catcher on those downs. LaFleur previously said that Love’s season-low route participation rate in Week 5 was partially due to his ankle injury. We may earn a commission when you buy through links on this page. The Vikings, which have yet to lose a game this season (6-0), feature both a bottom-10 offense (20.8 points/game) and the league's top defensive unit. Coordinated by Brian Flores, Minnesota's defense has permitted just 12.3 points a game, and hasn't allowed more than 16 points in a game since Week 2. And most recently, the Vikings surrendered just 10 points in a 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7. Additionally, Minnesota has been extremely stout against the pass thus far this season. In fact, Kevin O'Connell's squad has allowed the second-fewest passing yards (930) and the least amount of touchdowns through the air (three) through the season's first seven weeks. The Vikings have also already secured seven interceptions, spearheaded by cornerback Byron Murphy's league-high three picks. So, Lions signal-caller Jared Goff, who has yet to throw an interception in 2026, will face arguably his biggest test of the campaign against Minnesota's stingy pass defense . Then on the opposite side of the ball, Detroit's secondary will receive one of its toughest assignments of the year, going head-to-head with All-Pro wideout Justin Jefferson. Jefferson, who has surpassed 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first six NFL seasons, has accumulated 302 reception yards and three touchdowns in five games this season. He's unquestionably Vikings passer Kyler Murray's go-to target and one of the very best receivers in the game today. Subsequently, D.J. Reed, the Lions’ No. 1 cornerback , should get the majority of one-on-one reps with the Pro Bowl pass-catcher. Additionally, I wouldn't be surprised if Detroit defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard deployed a rotation of corners in the Week 8 tilt. And as a result, I could see the likes of Ennis Rakestraw and Roger McCreary also getting opportunities to defend Jefferson Sunday. It'll hardly be an easy task for the Lions’ defensive backs group. However, Detroit does have a solid track record against Jefferson, having limited him to under 60 yards the past three meetings between the NFC North rivals . And if the Lions could do it a fourth straight time, it would go a long way toward Dan Campbell's squad notching its fifth victory on the season. At this present juncture, I'm willing to give Detroit a 61 percent chance to secure the Week 8 victory . The 4-2 Detroit Lions are fresh off a thrilling, last-second 20-17 victory over the Green Bay Packers. They are set to host the league's final remaining undefeated juggernaut: the 6-0 Minnesota Vikings. This Week eight clash is a textbook battle of strengths. Head coach Dan Campbell has Jared Goff playing at an early-season MVP level, engineering an electric offense. Meanwhile, Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores is piloting a historic, blitz-heavy defensive unit that is suffocating opposing quarterbacks. With massive divisional implications on the line, here are three bold predictions for this highly anticipated rivalry game. 1. Jared Goff Extends Interception-Free Streak to 7 Games Despite Massive Blitz Brian Flores' defense leads the NFL in blitz percentage (38%) and thrives on turning ordinary passing downs into an absolute nightmare. The Vikings' defense has already forced 11 takeaways and racked up 21 sacks. Statistically, Flores loves to force opposing quarterbacks into hurried mistakes. The first bold prediction is that Jared Goff will throw for over 275 yards, multiple touchdowns, and maintain a completely clean sheet with zero turnovers. Goff is currently on an unbelievable heater, throwing 14 touchdowns to zero interceptions through six games. While Flores will throw a kitchen sink of disguised coverages and loaded fronts at him, Goff boasts a stellar 127.1 passer rating against the blitz this season. Shielded by one of the best offensive lines in football, Goff will stay calm in the pocket, pick apart the blitz, and keep the football safe. 2. Jahmyr Gibbs Cracks 120+ Rushing Yards The Vikings have given up very little through the air, ranking near the top of the league in passing defense. However, if their elite unit has a minor vulnerability, it is on the ground. Last week, the Indianapolis Colts exposed some cracks by carving up Minnesota for 154 rushing yards. The second bold prediction is that Jahmyr Gibbs will erupt for over 120 rushing yards and a touchdown. Gibbs has been an absolute workhorse for Detroit, averaging an astounding 103.3 rushing yards per game. Though Flores historically found success neutralizing Gibbs last season, Drew Petzing's offensive scheme will counter Minnesota's aggressive defensive stunts by leaning heavily on the ground game. Gibbs will tire out the Vikings' pass-rushers, hit the secondary at full speed, and log his biggest performance of the year. 3. Lions Hand the Vikings Their First Loss of the Season Minnesota's 6-0 start has been heavily reliant on their elite defense. Kyler Murray and the Vikings' offense have regularly stalled, ranking 29th in total yards per game and managing just 20.7 points per game. To make matters more difficult, starting running back Aaron Jones Sr. is severely limited with a knee injury. The final bold prediction is that the Detroit Lions will win a high-scoring thriller, handing Minnesota its first loss of the 2026 season. The returning presence of Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch gives Detroit's secondary the physical playmaking identity needed to keep Justin Jefferson under wraps. Ford Field will be deafening, and Detroit's offensive versatility will simply be too much to contain for all four quarters. Expect the Lions to walk away with a definitive statement win to tighten the race for the NFC North crown.

These teams meet in Week 8, and here are bold predictions for the NFC North clash. It's a critical game for the Lions. The NFC North could end up with only two playoff teams. That's because the 49ers, Seahawks, and Rams still seem like firm bets. And that leaves only one other Wild Card spot. The Lions stand at 4-2 while the Vikings are 6-0. A loss would leave the Lions three games back of first place with nearly half the season in the rearview mirror. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs will rush for 100-plus yards It's tough to throw against the Vikings. They rank No. 2 in the NFL against the pass, allowing just 155 yards per game. And while their run defense is good, it's still the better path to consistently moving the football. Gibbs is fourth in the NFL with 620 yards through six games. Look for the Lions to put a saddle on him against the Vikings. Yes, the Lions are clearly overusing Gibbs already. He's almost on a record pace , according to NBC Sports. "If Gibbs keeps to his current pace of 27.7 touches per game for the entire 17-game season, he'll finish this season with a whopping 470 touches," Michael David Smith wrote. "That would be the second-most in a season in NFL history, second only to former James Wilder, who had 492 touches with the 1984 Buccaneers." Gibbs should get close to that number of touches on the ground alone. He had 29 carries against the Saints and Packers this season. Look for the neighborhood of 25 against the Vikings. He's averaging 4.6 per carry, so that easily puts him over 100. And don't worry about the injury scare late against the Packers, according to mlive.com. During his postgame media session, Lions coach Dan Campbell confirmed that Gibbs is OK and avoided serious injury . "Yeah, we got him checked," Lions head coach Dan Campbell said. "He should be good. That's that whole, 'Is it really worth going down and try to finish the game, or you just go score?' Sometimes I question that. I don't know, maybe we shouldn't just, but all good. It's a good win." Lions will double the Vikings' season average in points allowed For the season, the Vikings are allowing just 12.3 points per game. Over the last three games, they are giving up just 33 points. But the Lions will hit them for 24-plus points. Not only will Gibbs cut loose, but his runs will set up play-action daggers for Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. This is no timid prediction. The Vikings defense is the real deal. The players will even tell you that , according to The Athletic. "It's a generational group," cornerback Isaiah Rodgers said. "We've got guys who go out and trust the scheme. They trust (Flores and his staff). The stats speak for themselves." Defensive tackle Levi Drake Rodriguez said it is togetherness that brings the good outcomes. "Hopefully, that showed the joy we have on the field with each other," Rodriguez said. "We want to work hard for each other. We want to be right." But the Lions are a different beast. They are king of the offensive jungle for a reason. They rank No. 2 in the NFL with 397.3 yards per game. The NFL used to be a league where great defense would pretty much always shut down a great offense. But the rules have changed. And the Lions will cut loose for a point total the Vikings haven't allowed since 22 in the season opener against the Packers. Vikings QB Kyler Murray will have his best game of the season For all the Lions are on offense, they ain't that on defense. They rank dead last in the league with 391 yards allowed per game. Murray hasn't thrown for 250 yards in a game yet this season. In fact, he hasn't done it since 2024. And he only has three touchdown passes in basically four games played. He missed almost all of the season opener after a first-quarter injury. But the Lions are relatively decent against the run. They are an open gate against the pass. And Murray will take advantage with some chunk plays down the field. Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell is standing behind Murray, according to The Athletic. "I think our guys are very confident that we're not far off," O'Connell said. "The far-off changes a little bit as you go, but I'm very, very confident we'll get it going." One reason for optimism is that Murray has gotten better at play action. The Vikings used play action on nearly half of Murray's dropbacks in Week 7. And Murray hit on eight of 11 passes. There's still hope for Murray. Some people have been writing him off and saying the Vikings should move on, but this is a chance for him to silence critics.
