Earlier in the week, Dan Campbell described the Minnesota defense as good as it gets. " Brian (Flores) is doing a hell of a job. This thing, they play very complementary football. Everything is fueled by this defense. That's the starting point." Over seven weeks this season, the Vikings' potent combination of LBs Blake Cashman and Andrew Van Ginkle, along with IDL Jalen Redmond, and EDGE Dallas Turner, led the league with an astounding 70.8 blitz rate . The Vikings' defense posted the league's highest pressure and sack rate, while allowing the lowest passer completion percentage in the NFL. Although Detroit boasts the NFL's second-highest scoring offense, averaging 30.66 points per game this season, the team faces a daunting challenge, taking on the mercurial Flores-designed defense. The Lions' success will depend on how well the newly re-configured offensive line can divert and delay the Vikings' punishing defense. Detroit Lions offensive tackle Blake Miller (76) and offensive lineman Tate Ratledge (69) block Arizona Cardinals defensive lineman Walter Nolen III (97) during the first half at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona, on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026. The Challenge of Facing the Number 1 Ranked Defense Flores is one of the NFL's most enterprising defense coordinators who has earned a reputation for constantly changing things up to stymie opposing teams. His unpredictable Vikings defense forces multiple turnovers and generates mass confusion to limit the opposition's chances of scoring. The Minnesota defense in 2026 has held opposing offenses to an average of 12.33 points per game. The 5-2 Chicago Bears were held to a mere three points in Week 2, but the other teams the Vikings faced this season include the 1-5 Miami Dolphins, the 2-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the 2-5 New Orleans Saints, and the 2-5 Indianapolis Colts. The Vikings' defense has yet to face an offense comparable to the caliber of Detroit's high-powered offense. Dan Campbell remembers only too well how the Vikings' defense hurt the Lions a year ago. He admitted, "They did a hell of a job against us last year. They got after us. We turned the ball over, and we didn't make enough plays. They did, and we've got to play a hell of a lot better this year. That's the no-brainer statement there." "The Vikings defense understands how the system works," Campbell said, "and they use it to their advantage against the opposition." "They understand where they're going to exploit you at and then where you're trying to, 'OK, this is where my outlet is.' They take that away, too. They exploit you and then take away your outlet. They just create havoc and chaos. And inevitably, what they want, and have done consistently, is they force you to make massive errors…Turnovers, massive turnovers, so it's third-and-32. And that's where they want you, way behind the sticks." Oct 11, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints tight end Juwan Johnson (83) carries the ball against Minnesota Vikings linebacker Blake Cashman (51) during the second half at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images A Vastly Improved Detroit Lions Offensive Line Recognizing the Lions' disappointing 2025 season was largely due to a weakened, ineffective offensive line, Brad Holmes made rebuilding the offensive line his top priority. His smart, savvy acquisitions through free agency and the 2026 NFL Draft provided offensive line coach Hank Fraley with a significantly improved quality of offensive line talent. Holmes acquired versatile veteran lineman Juice Scruggs through the David Montgomery trade, signed free agent center Cade Mays, and drafted 2026 NFL Draft first-round pick, Blake Miller. The new trio joins All-Pro tackle Penei Sewell, Christian Mahogany, and Tate Ratledge to form the core of a newly reconfigured offensive line that could regain the success of previous years. Under Fraley's leadership in 2023 and 2024, the Lions' offensive line had been one of the NFL's best, ranked 2nd in the NFL with 8,864 rushing yards and 91 rushing touchdowns. In addition, Detroit's offensive line did an impressive job protecting Goff, and allowed the fourth fewest sacks (124) during that time span. Now, armed with the talent capable of producing similar results, the Lions are poised to knock the current NFC North division leaders off their top spot. Oct 11, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Detroit Lions offensive line/ run game coordinator Hank Fraley against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Preseason Hiccups It takes time for a new offensive line to gel, and the Lions' preseason had its share of hiccups. Miller, the rookie right guard, cut his teeth going against All-Pro Aidan Hutchinson day after day. He got knocked down, pushed around, but to his credit, Miller got right back up, dusted himself off, and learned from his mistakes. Mays had been acquired to be the Lions' starting center, but after he fractured his wrist in the preseason, Scruggs stepped up and performed admirably. Through the first five weeks of the season, he earned a 75.6 PFF grade and ranked first among all 32 NFL centers. After the trials and tribulations of the 2025 season, Fraley once again has a group of talented players who can rise to the challenge of taking on the NFL's top defenses. However, this will be the o-line's biggest test to date. Oct 11, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Detroit Lions offensive lineman Juice Scruggs (70) prepares to snap the ball to quarterback Jared Goff (16) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images It All Starts With the Lions' Offensive Line Recently, Detroit's MVP candidate quarterback, Jared Goff, was asked how much he credits his success to the Lions' offensive line. Goff responded , "Oh, a ton. All of it. We can't do anything without those guys. We do have a really good skill group here, but they know, and we know as an offense, and as a team, we only go where they go. And so when they're playing well, we can do some pretty special things, and they know that." Coach Campbell agrees. However, as excited as he is already about the success of the Lions' offensive line this season, he expects we'll continue to see improvement ."But man, there are some things we are definitely getting better at. I'm excited about this O-line playing together. I mentioned this before, but now that we've kind of got those guys going here, we can get this five settled in and let them just soak them with reps together in real games and let them grow." The Last Word Sunday's game will undoubtedly come down to a ferocious battle in the trenches as the Minnesota defense does its best to pressure Goff, who holds the leagues-second highest passer rating of 112.5. Goff also leads the NFL with 14 passing touchdowns and one rushing touchdown with zero interceptions over 1,788 passing yards. Last year, despite the limitations of the Lions' offensive line, Goff attained the elite production of over 4,500 passing yards. With the significantly improved coverage of Detroit's offensive line and the dual-headed threat posed by premier running back Jahmyr Gibbs, the majority of experts predict that Minnesota's talented defense will be in for a long and frustrating afternoon. away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Lions, Kerby Joseph had his 3-week window to return from the PUP list opened this week, but he is unlikely to play on Sunday. Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown did not practice Wednesday with shoulder and ankle injuries, respectively, which is something to keep an eye on the rest of the week. For the Vikings, Kevin O'Connell didn't seem overly concerned about either Aaron Jones or Joe Huber. "Aaron Jones, Joe Huber, and Gavin Bartholomew are off the injury report and good to go for Sunday, per Kevin O'Connell," Will Ragatz reported via X . "Depth safety Jay Ward is questionable." Jones was nothing short of heroic over the month that Mason was out, carrying a workload that equalled nearly 25 touches per game despite his injury history and playing in his age-32 season — through an MCL sprain for part of that stretch, no less. Jones' status for Minnesota's upcoming showdown with the Detroit Lions at Ford Field has been in question for the last several days because of the knee issue. However, on Friday, October 30, head coach Kevin O'Connell confirmed that Jones will be a full-go in Detroit on Sunday. And that wasn't the only bit of positive injury news for the Vikings. Vikings Must Improve Run Game to Prop Up Struggling Pass Attack Getty Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson . "He's our best player, and we've got to find a way to continue to activate him," O'Connell said of Jefferson . "We just haven't really see teams say, ‘You know what? We're gonna get that eighth defender around the line of scrimmage with so much conviction that we're willing to allow [Jefferson] to have one-on-ones.' When he's had them, he's won." Having Mason back healthy alongside Jones affords the Vikings the two-headed offensive backfield they envisioned coming into the season, but it has not necessarily been a dynamic duo. If Minnesota is going to get a win this weekend, they'll likely need to prevent Gibbs and the Lions from becoming their fourth opponent of 2026 to finish a game with at least 120 rushing yards. T.J. home.blurb: Currently, the Lions have utilized Sione Vaki as the second option. Isiah Pacheco, a veteran who came to Detroit on a one-year deal after four seasons in Kansas City, is on injured reserve after having a back procedure and expected to be out until December. Could Detroit Lions Make Surprise Trade to Add Depth Behind Jahmyr Gibbs? Skip to main content SI.COM The Detroit Lions have one of the NFL's brightest young stars in running back Jahmyr Gibbs. Through the first six games of the season, Gibbs has once again proven why he's viewed across the NFL landscape as one of the top talents at the position. His blend of exciting speed and physicality have shown up plenty, and he's been consistent after being essentially handed the reins to the offense when the Lions traded David Montgomery in the offseason. However, in this six-game stretch to start the season a troubling trend has emerged. Gibbs has been a workhorse in every sense of the word, currently ranking third in rushing attempts (134) and first in total touches (166) to start the year. With how dynamic and explosive Gibbs is, the prevailing fear is that the team could overuse him which would in turn lead to some of that explosiveness being sapped late in the year. While Gibbs has handled the workload well to this point, and impressed coaches with how effective he has been able to be, one wonders if this is sustainable over the duration of an NFL season plus a potential playoff run. With an ESPN report earlier in the week stating that the Lions have remained in contact with free agent running back Kareem Hunt after bringing him in for a visit during training camp, it's worth exploring the possibility of the Lions making a deal for running back depth to help offset Gibbs' workload. Appearing in all six games, Vaki has totaled 16 carries for 56 yards while also serving as an option in pass-protection on passing downs for the offense. With the Nov. 10 trade deadline approaching, the Lions have the ability to seek some help from elsewhere to add a veteran option who could give them some production and take a portion of the work off of Gibbs' shoulders. Some of the top names being floated around at the position can likely be written off as potential Lions targets, with those being Indianapolis' Jonathon Taylor and Philadelphia's Saquon Barkley. However, there are some other intriguing candidates that could fit the Lions' need for depth. Here are three potential trade targets the Lions could evaluate adding in the event that they want to bolster their depth at running back. Tampa Bay's Kenny Gainwell and Tennessee's Tony Pollard are two potential trade candidates who currently play for struggling teams. While the Buccaneers appear to have gotten some momentum after a thrashing of Carolina, Gainwell is behind young budding star Bucky Irving and could be an asset they'd be comfortable dealing for a late-round draft pick. Next week, the team will have him participate much more in practice sessions. "He's progressing well. I do think there's a chance we could get him back in late December," said Campbell. "He's put a tremendous amount of work in. He's doing pretty good." Safety Thomas Harper has been on the injured reserve list after suffering an ankle injury against the Buffalo Bills. Sheppard noticed the impact the former Alabama Crimson Tide defender had on his teammates in a Week 7 home victory. “I think the effect he had on his teammates. One of my favorite things from that game, I don't know if you guys caught this, go back and watch it. It's super cool. On his interception, he's still backpedaling. And right when he opens his hip, the ball's launched. And Chuck Clark, before BB opens his hip, raises his hand," said Sheppard. "And this is what I mean when I say affecting the teammates. He raises his hand. When he sees BB open his hip, he puts both hands in the air. I mean, I've never seen that. I'm like, 'Chuck, you run to the ball.' Nope, the play's over. "And just what that does for teammates, what that did, the swagger it brings, knowing you have an enforcer who can go cover the number one receiver. BB's a rare player in this league. Neither team is looking too hot at the moment. The Raiders are on a four-game losing streak and the Jets just lost to the previously winless Dolphins . To get a feel for how this one could play out, we get the takes from the Raiders Wire staff. Game picks for Raiders Week 8 matchup vs Jets Lance Fernandez -- Jets 24, Raiders 20 The Jets have struggled offensively, ranking in the bottom half in passing yards, rushing yards, and points per game. However, playing against a defense that has surrendered the fourth-most points per game and playing at home should give New York's offense a boost. That and the Jets' solid pass defense should keep the Raiders' losing streak going. Marvin Uzor -- Raiders 24, Jets 20 The Jets have been the NFL's slowest-starting offense since last season, so this is the week the Raiders finally don't have to dig out of an early hole. And they're coming off handing the Dolphins their first win of the season. The same Dolphins team the Raiders put a hurting on in the opener. I see a close one here. away.headline: Jets’ Braelon Allen upgraded on injury report before Raiders game, but Breece Hall is not
away.blurb: Allen, who was limited on Wednesday with an ankle injury, was a full participant in Thursday's practice, according to the team's official injury report. Meanwhile, Hall, nursing a quadriceps injury, was limited for the second straight practice this week. He suffered the quad strain in Week 3 versus the Detroit Lions and has missed the last four games. Elsewhere on the injury report, left guard Dylan Parham (knee) was limited for a second straight day. Courtesy of Wednesday's practice report , defensive back Doneiko Slaughter was listed as a non-participant with a hamstring injury. Slaughter was not listed on the Week 7 practice report, and it is not known when he picked up this new hamstring injury. Slaughter, who played collegiate football at Tennessee (2020–2023) and Arkansas (2024), began his NFL career as an undrafted free agent with the Jacksonville Jaguars . Slaughter would later sign a reserve/future contract with the Steelers in January 2026. He was unfortunately released during final roster cuts but subsequently signed with the Steelers' practice squad. Slaughter was elevated from the practice squad for the Steelers' first three games of the season and was signed to the active roster on October 1. He was later waived but ultimately brought back on October 10, where he now remains a vital depth contributor on the 53-man roster. picks.blurb: NFL predictions: Browns-Steelers square off in meaningful midseason match-up for once - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING NFL injury tracker live updates Ja out at least 4 weeks New head for D-Wade statue Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Chris Pokorny Fri, October 30, 2026 at 3:21 PM UTC · 13 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns (5-2) take on the Pittsburgh Steelers (5-2). Below, we analyze a few advantages, disadvantages, or general thoughts about the two teams before getting to our predictions for the game. It's Been 23 Years | Getty Images If I could put the meme from the Titanic here, I would, with respect to it having been 23 years (which is a 22-game losing streak) since the Cleveland Browns have won a road game against the Pittsburgh Steelers in the regular season. We'll always have that playoff victory over them, but we're trying to keep focused on the unfathomable statistic of losing 22 in a row somewhere. Of course, the reason for that has largely been that the Browns have been a bad football team, while Pittsburgh has generally been good. But, it's not like Cleveland hasn't been able to beat Pittsburgh during that stretch at all. In fact, at home since 2003, the Browns are 10-13-1, including winning 7 of their last 8 games there. On the road, they are 1-22, with 22 straight losses. That 2003 match-up was one featuring Tim Couch as the Browns' starting quarterback, as he went 20-of-25 for 208 yards, 2 TD, 1 INT, and 1 rushing TD in a 33-13 victory. Cleveland still have the classic quartet of Kevin Johnson , Quincy Morgan , Andre' Davis , and Dennis Northcutt as their receivers, with Steve Heiden as their primary tight end. William Green ran 33 times for 115 yards. Pittsburgh was led by Tommy Maddox at quarterback, with Amos Zereoue and Jerome Bettis running and Hines Ward , Plaxico Burress , and Antwaan Randle El as their receivers. Phil Dawson was putting kicks through the uprights for the Browns. I was 14 years old back then, just starting high school. I'm 37 now, having been through college, had a full-time job for awhile, and started a family. It's time we turned the corner for the Browns, isn't it? Home-away records sometimes seem less valuable these days. I could go into context and say that Cleveland's 2-2 road record this year was the team just not being prepared in Week 1, and also because of sloppy rain conditions against the Jets, and not because 'they weren't at home.' But when you just look at the records straight up, the Browns are 3-0 at home. Also 3-0 at home this year? The Pittsburgh Steelers, with wins over the Falcons, Bengals, and Colts. They, like Cleveland, have had a relatively soft schedule this year, but it's let them build some confidence and work out some things too. This game won't be easy, but I'm excited for it. Those Darn Slow Starts Last week, I harped on the Browns needing to get their offense rocking, especially with KC Concepcion , and also needed the defense to stop allowing opening-drive scores. Cleveland accomplished half of that with the offense taking off, but the defense found themselves in a 14-0 hole before getting things back on track. Thinking back to the first Steelers game, Pittsburgh began the game with a 17-play, 73-yard drive that took up 9:48 of game clock. Then, until the fourth quarter, their drives were: interception, punt, missed field goal, field goal, punt, punt, and punt. It's always been a known factor in the NFL that some teams can have greater success on their first drive with well-scripted sequences. But it's a bit mind-blowing that this defense can play so well the rest of the game — which I've attributed to Mike Rutenburg's ability to make adjustments — but they can't get that stop, even out of dumb luck, on the first drive. I know Rutenburg would say that it doesn't matter if that touchdown drive comes on the opening drive, or the fifth drive, they want to stop it. But setting the tone early will be a factor as some of these games get more serious. The last time these teams played, Cleveland erupted for 21 straight points in the second quarter. That isn't going to happen every week (even though they erupted for 17 points in a row just last week, after being in a hole…) Here are some other notes: The running game was encouraging last week. I like some of the little things we're seeing improve with team blocking, and I also like the adjustment to go under center more. I think Cleveland, in their efforts to make Deshaun Watson comfortable, have often gone from Shotgun, which can hurt the running game at times. Watson has been much more unphased this year, and I think we're seeing how being under center can add some things to the ground game, quick passing game, and even springing someone like KC Concepcion open off of playaction. Speaking of Concepcion, the usage of him last week was picture perfect. Keep doing it — he is the one guy who can really propel this offense to the next level, and help open things up for other guys too. The number of crossing routes that Cleveland has started taking advantage of is perfect too. Jaylen Warren is the guy who the Browns need to stop. He's averaging 5.5 yards per carry on the season, and with the return of Rico Dowdle last week, the duo has been very effective on the ground. I still fear Darnell Washington to a degree. The big tight end had a touchdown catch against the Browns, and has a touchdown catch in each of the past two games. I'd be tempted to put Emmanuel McNeil-Warren on him at times to see what happens. The big X-Factor this week that could throw a wrench in Cleveland's chances is the fact that Tytus Howard might be out with a concussion. That would put Dawand Jones in as the starting right tackle. We all remember back in 2023, when Jones — in limited action — 'shut down' T.J. Watt , which got everyone excited about Jones' future. It's been a bit rough since then, and with injuries and lesser playing time, Jones hasn't looked very sharp during fill-in duty. And then what happens if Jones goes down with an injury? I'm assuming that KT Leveston will be a gameday elevation from the practice squad, but remember, he was outright cut after being a contender for the starting right guard job in camp. Cleveland drafted Austin Barber to be a reserve offensive tackle, but he's flourished at right guard. I suppose the they could shift Barber to right tackle, Elgton Jenkins to right guard, and then put Luke Wypler at center. On paper, that works for me. However, with the continuity these guys have built up, would they want to switch three linemen as opposed to just one? Fingers crossed that Jones not only stays healthy, but plays has a solid outing. According to FanDuel , the Browns are 3.5 point underdogs against the Steelers. The over/under is 39.5. Quick Hitters Offensive coordinator Travis Switzer was asked about if the running game so a breakthrough this past week, but he just appreciated the collective effort and improvements on first and second down: "Yeah, I mean, I think a lot of the things, we have been seeing improvement over the last couple weeks, so it was great to see the production that we had on Sunday. As far as breakthrough, I don't know. I don't know that any of our guys really look at it that way. I think that the things that we've been emphasizing to improve, we've been. We were a lot better on first and second down, which allowed us to get more runs called. You know, the more you're on schedule, the more you'll be able to run the ball. So, as far as breakthrough, I don't know. I mean, we were certainly really happy to see the production that we did, and we'll continue to try to improve." Defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg wouldn't really give an answer to the slow start of the defense each week, other than they treat every drive the same as far as diagnosing what went wrong behind closed doors: In everything we do, when it is to our collective standard, we are constantly trying to get it better. So, whether it's the first drive, something else, something we're doing really well, it's a constant under construction through the week of why, tell the truth, try and figure it out together and fight our a—- off really to fix it. And it's a really cool process, collectively, as a staff and players." Special teams coordinator Bryon Storer was asked about a couple strategic elements, and I'm going to post two quotes from him this week, because I appreciate the insight. The first was what happened on the 12-men penalty on the punt that led to a Titans first down, and then later, he talked about the two touchbacks by Andre Szmyt to start the game: "Absolutely. [Monken] got every right to be angry about that situation, and that ultimately falls on my shoulders, 100%. So, I take full responsibility for the 12 men on the field. I've got to catch that. So, the situation was, it was fourth-and-one. And in a fourth-and-one situation, we don't usually go with our normal punt return team. It's our safe team, as they like to say it, and it's majority of defensive players, all defensive players on the field. So, in that situation, you're thinking about fake the whole time. And going into the game, we are very 'fake' aware that there could potentially be a fake run against us. So, in all honesty, we had the safe team out there, and one of our punt return players stayed on the field. We were so fake aware in that moment, we failed to notice that there was 12 men on the field. And so, it just cannot happen. It's a big-time learning lesson for me as a coach. And then we addressed it with the guys, we instituted a few different fail-safes to make sure that never happens again, because that absolutely cannot happen again moving forward." "So, we're going to kick it to him. And so, but I did tell Dre (Andre Szmyt) he could be a little bit more aggressive, because we'd rather have it more towards the goal line versus being caught on the five-to-10-yard line and have him have a full head of steam with basically one cut. So, I told him, 'hey, you can be more aggressive toward the goal line.' After the first one, I said, hey, Dre, no big deal. You know, we'll get him the next one. And then the second time I was a little bit more disappointed. Said, Dre, we can't do that twice now. So, our whole philosophy going into that game was to cover kicks, and so we would rather not kick touchbacks in those situations." picks.blurb: Falcons vs. Buccaneers Expert Pick | NFL Week 8 2026 Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE KREWE MEMBERS The national analysts are leaning towards the Falcons in Sunday's NFC South showdown at Raymond James Stadium, but some expect a motivated Baker Mayfield to swing the balance Scott Smith Senior Writer/Editor The Tampa Bay Buccaneers come back home in Week Eight trying to turn a rousing road victory at Carolina into a streak within NFC South divisional play, as the Atlanta Falcons visit on Sunday. The Falcons are also riding high, having dispatched a previously unbeaten San Francisco 49ers team last Sunday, and they bring serious firepower to Raymond James Stadium in the quartet of Michael Penix, Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts. To find out how to watch, listen and livestream the game, click here . Several analysts noted that both teams want to run the ball but will be facing defenses that are hard to run against. One analyst called the two squads "mirror images" in their strengths and weaknesses. One reporter suggested this was a Baker Mayfield game – that his performance would swing the balance – and that he might have some extra motivation going against a Kevin Stefanski-led team. Another pointed out that both teams have struggled to make winning plays at the very end of one-score games, and yet another thought the possible return of Emeka Egbuka for the Bucs would be significant. Perhaps the expert who put it best was the one who called it a "box of chocolates" game with these two teams: You never know what you're going to get. Bleacher Report's Ian Hanford sided with the Falcons in a tight matchup and explains why: "Both the Falcons and Buccaneers have stellar run defenses, so this game may come down to which QB plays better. The Bucs beat the Panthers in Baker Mayfield's return to the field, but that was more about leaning on the run game than Mayfield steering the ship. Yes, with Carolina losing Thursday night to Green Bay, no team in the NFC South is even .500. Atlanta sits tied with Carolina entering the weekend, while Tampa Bay sits just one game back despite losing its first four games. Atlanta snapped a two-game losing streak last Sunday with arguably its best win of the season, knocking off the previously unbeaten 49ers, 29-20. Michael Penix Jr. completed 25 of 34 passes for 213 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, throwing scoring passes to Nick Muse , Kyle Pitts Sr . and Drake London , while Atlanta’s defense produced four takeaways and scored 13 points off San Francisco turnovers. Penix has helped stabilize the Falcons after their 0-2 start, and Sunday represents a homecoming for the Tampa-area native. Tampa Bay, meanwhile, dismantled Carolina 43-13 last week in Baker Mayfield’s return after missing three games with a dislocated thumb. The Bucs own the league’s third-ranked rushing attack and they played to their strength against the Panthers attempting only 11 passes while piling up 258 rushing yards on 49 carries. Bucky Irving ran for a chunk of the 258 yards totaling 106 yards and two touchdowns. Tampa’s defense added four takeaways and five sacks. The Falcons’ defensive front and playmaking secondary were difference-makers against San Francisco, but Tampa Bay has topped 240 rushing yards in two of its last three victories and with Emeka Egbuka declared OUT of Sunday’s game, the Bucs will look to their run game to be the difference-maker against a Falcons’ team that will undoubtedly stack the box. away.blurb: Fortunately, the Buccaneers received some encouraging news on the injury front just in time for the pivotal matchup. Several key players are trending toward a return, giving Tampa Bay a chance to take the field with its healthiest roster in weeks. The Buccaneers released their injury report after practice on Thursday, and several designations stood out. Antoine Winfield Jr. was a full participant after missing the last three games with a fractured rib , and the star safety is gearing up for a return. Heading into a matchup against a stacked Falcons offense featuring Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, the importance of Winfield's return can't be overstated. home.headline: Buccaneers expect Baker Mayfield back, rule out three starters
home.blurb: The Buccaneers' official Friday injury report lists wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, right tackle Luke Goedeke, and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. as ruled out. Baker Mayfield remains questionable with a right thumb injury, although head coach Todd Bowles expects him to start against Carolina. Getting Mayfield back would significantly boost an offense that has struggled to establish consistency. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels has done a respectable job given his limited NFL experience, but Mayfield's ability to recognize pressure, adjust protections, and make pre-snap decisions gives offensive coordinator Zac Robinson more flexibility. However, Tampa Bay's offense will be far from full strength on Sunday. Egbuka missed Wednesday and Thursday's practices with concussion and foot injuries before returning Friday in a limited capacity. Despite the improvement, the team ruled him out for Sunday's game. His absence removes one of Tampa Bay's primary receiving threats from an offense that has already struggled to create consistent opportunities downfield. Goedeke also returned to practice in a limited capacity Friday after missing the previous two sessions with a calf injury. He was ultimately ruled out, leaving Tampa Bay without its starting right tackle. Protecting Mayfield will be especially important if he returns against a Carolina defense looking to exploit an offensive line that has struggled this season. Defensively, Winfield will miss Sunday's game with a rib injury. The veteran safety was limited all week but couldn't return to game action. His absence adds to the challenge for a young defense that has shown encouraging signs despite Tampa Bay's 1-5 record. Carolina will also deal with injuries, particularly on its defensive front. Outside linebackers Jaelan Phillips and Thomas Incoom were ruled out after missing all three practices. Offensive tackle Monroe Freeling and linebacker Bam Martin-Scott are questionable despite participating fully throughout the week. The Buccaneers enter Sunday's game looking to rebound from a 26-19 overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Mayfield's expected return gives Tampa Bay reason to be optimistic, but the absences of Egbuka, Goedeke, and Winfield will force the team to adjust on both sides of the ball. The Indianapolis Colts come to EverBank Stadium on Sunday with a quarterback who goes down a lot. Indianapolis (2-5) has lost three straight, fired general manager Chris Ballard and then traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner on Tuesday. Jacksonville (4-2) comes off a 34-31 loss to Houston in London and has won the last two meetings in the series. "This has to all be about our improvements, us getting back on track," head coach Liam Coen said Wednesday, per the team's website . The Jaguars are a big home favorite . away.headline: Quenton Nelson, Colts were close to a contract extension in the offseason, per report
away.blurb: In return for the All-Pro guard, the Colts received a 2027 third round pick and 2028 fifth round pick from Seattle. Indianapolis Zoo workers unionize as zoo works to restore accreditation, replace CEO News Sports Things To Do Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals COLTS Quenton Nelson, Colts were close to a contract extension in the offseason, per report Cameron Cocquyt Indianapolis Star Oct. 29, 2026, 1:39 p.m. ET The Indianapolis Colts traded guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks following the firing of general manager Chris Ballard. Nelson had reportedly wanted to sign a long-term contract extension to remain with the Colts. In exchange for Nelson, Indianapolis received a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. After the Indianapolis Colts fired general manger Chris Ballard 10 days ago, it sent a ripple effect down the organization. Coming off a second-half letdown and loss to the then 0-5 Tennessee Titans , it seemed clear that changes were imminent. Tuesday, the Colts traded Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks , a franchise cornerstone on the offensive line since Indianapolis drafted him with the No. 6 pick in the 2018 NFL Draft . With uncertainty surrounding the future of the organization, rumors began to swirl about trade requests regarding some of the Colts' most important players. ESPN NFL insider Ian Rapoport joined the Pat McAfee show Wednesday and shed some light on Nelson's situation in Indianapolis. "Is that accurate? He wanted to get a deal done with Indianapolis this off-season," McAfee asked Rapoport. "Yeah, that is true." Rapoport replied. "When Chris Ballard was there, I really thought it was going to get done." Nelson didn't sign an extension. He is currently on the final year of a four-year, $80 million contract, his first large-scale extension following his rookie contract. According to Rapoport, it was up to Nelson if he would be spending the next several years with the Colts' organization. "This is a huge bounty for someone in the middle of the season," Rapoport added. "A lot of people wanted this guy that the Seahawks think is like really, really going to help their run game." Since arriving in Indianapolis, Nelson was selected to the Pro Bowl each of his eight seasons and was named an All-Pro in six of those. Just a short time after Nelson's trade, the Colts moved another key piece of the roster in DeForest Buckner , who returns to the organization that drafted him, the San Francisco 49ers . Indianapolis received a 2027 fourth-round pick. With uncertainty surrounding the organization, there is reason to believe the roster moves won't stop here. Nonetheless, it was an offensive pillar that may have set off a revolving door of player personnel in Indianapolis. We may earn a commission when you buy through links on this page. away.headline: Colts cut veteran as injury report helps linebacker depth, hurts cornerbacks
away.blurb: Tight ends Tyler Warren (groin) and Drew Ogletree (knee) were both limited in practice for the second consecutive day. Warren, the team leader in receptions, has missed the last two weeks with the groin injury, and he was somewhat optimistic that he’ll be able to go against the Jaguars. Rookie linebacker CJ Allen is expected to start after recovering from an ankle injury, leading to the release of veteran Germaine Pratt. Cornerback Sauce Gardner returned to full practice, offering a potential solution to injuries in the secondary. INDIANAPOLIS — The Colts have made a flurry of roster moves this week, trying to cover a rash of injuries at the cornerback position while shoring up depth at linebacker. Rookie middle linebacker CJ Allen was a full participant in practice for the second consecutive day after missing last week’s game due to an ankle injury, although his fellow rookie, Bryce Boettcher, missed his second consecutive day with a groin injury. Indianapolis feels confident enough in its linebacker group to release veteran Germaine Pratt, who was signed to the practice squad two weeks ago but no longer has a path to playing time. Pratt played 20 snaps against Minnesota this week due to injuries, but the Colts plan to move Allen into the starting lineup now that he’s healthy. Pratt was a starter for 12 games in Indianapolis in 2025; the Colts are trying to get younger and faster at the position. “C.J. was going to start this week before he had that injury,” defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo said. “I think they’re all putting their time in, and the more at bats they get, the better they’re going to be.” The Colts have larger issues at cornerback. Sauce Gardner practiced in full for the first time since suffering a calf injury against Tennessee, offering a potential starting option. Indianapolis placed Cam Taylor-Britt on injured reserve earlier this week, and Justin Walley missed the second consecutive day with a knee injury. picks.headline: Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8
picks.blurb: Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING NFL injury tracker live updates Ja out at least 4 weeks New head for D-Wade statue Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 Ben Strauss, ClutchPoints Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:26 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFL teams based in Los Angeles are not having a great first half of the 2026 NFL season. Both the Chargers and Rams combined have three wins on the season headed into Week 8. The Rams are doing all of the heavy lifting here, but even they are having a disappointing season compared to their offseason expectations. It seems a Rams vs. Chargers Super Bowl is not in the cards this season. While both teams have been frustrating, they are in completely different situations ahead of Week 8. The Rams are very much alive in the NFC playoff race, but they need to continue stacking wins to remain competitive. Meanwhile, the Chargers are 0-6 and somehow still think they'll compete by the end of the season. This game means a lot for both teams, but the Rams arguably have much more to lose. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So which team will come out on top in this one? Here are three bold predictions ahead of this Battle for Los Angeles in Week 8 between the Chargers and Rams. Rams, Chargers combine for more rushing yards than passing yards Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Both LA teams built their teams to have a strong running game. Jim Harbaugh is known for his love of pounding the rock. The Chargers drafted Omarion Hampton and built a massive offensive line for that very reason. As for the Rams, Sean McVay has always leaned heavily on the running game dating back to the Todd Gurley years. That has continued into 2026, as the Rams popularized 13 personnel usage and have taken to a new level this season. But just how committed are they to running the ball? When both teams combine their final stats, this game will feature more rushing yards than passing yards. That sounds like a crazy prediction on the surface. So exactly how bold is this prediction? The Rams average roughly 70 more passing yards than rushing yards per game this season, compared to an 82-yard gap for the Chargers. So it would be quite shocking if both teams overcame this 152-yard difference. If this happens, it may require both defenses to ball out against the pass and allow a handful of explosive runs. This is definitely bold, but crazier things have happened. The Chargers dominate the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball If the Chargers are going to have a chance to win this game, they'll have to do so in the trenches. The injury situation for both teams makes this look like a strong possibility. Joe Alt is expected to return from injury for this game. One offensive lineman won't magically turn LA's o-line into an elite unit. However, it could do wonders as he still projects as an elite talent at the position. If the Chargers can count on one side of the line protected, they can always pull out some tricks to protect the other side. It is also important to note that the Rams have only managed 10 sacks in seven games played this season. That puts them at 27th in the NFL and only ahead of pitiful defensive teams like the Dolphins, Eagles, and Cowboys. It really shows that Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, and Poona Ford are injured. Flipping to the other side, the Chargers and Rams look pretty evenly matched in the trenches. The Rams may hold a slight lead, but nothing too crazy. Ultimately, the Chargers' formula for winning this game is predicated on winning the trenches. This is certainly an area where they could gain an advantage. The Chargers will keep Justin Herbert completely clean, not allowing a single sack. Meanwhile, they will sack Matthew Stafford at least twice. That may not be a huge advantage, but it gives the Chargers a fighting chance. Chargers take Rams to overtime, but lose by a field goal Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images It is really tempting to predict that the Chargers will get their first win of the season in this spot. But it just seems too far-fetched. Realistically, the Rams and Chargers are in two completely different worlds on offense. The Rams average more total yards per game than any other team, while the Chargers are statistically a bottom five offense. There's no reason to suggest that will change in Week 8. Furthermore, the Rams absolutely must win this game to stay alive in the NFC playoff race. McVay may be willing to pull out all the stops if this game becomes close, and the Chargers would need to be lucky to survive in that situation. But playing for pride is important too, so the Chargers won't go down without a fight. They just don't have the horses to get the job done. Brandon McManus kicks a game-winning field goal in overtime, cementing himself as the Rams' kicker for the rest of the season. He has 32 pressures, seventh among edge defenders, according to PFF . On Sunday at SoFi Stadium, he gets a Chargers offense that can’t keep Justin Herbert upright. Los Angeles (3-4) won 35-21 in Las Vegas last week, and Matthew Stafford passed Roman Gabriel for the franchise record in touchdown passes. The Rams still sit third in the NFC West . The Chargers are 0-6 and coming off a bye, but Rams head coach Sean McVay isn’t buying the record. “I really couldn’t care less what the record says,” McVay said Wednesday, per the team’s website . The Rams are a 6.5-point favorite in the battle for Inglewood. Here are four bold predictions. Byron Young sacks Justin Herbert twice The Rams have only 10 sacks, tied for 27th, per NFL.com , and we wrote before Week 7 about how they pressure plenty but don’t finish . Young has five sacks by PFF’s count. CBS Sports credits him with 4.5. Herbert has been sacked 21 times, tied for the fifth-most in the league, and 21.2% of his pressures have turned into sacks, according to PFF . Guard Kayode Awosika missed practice Wednesday and Thursday with a fibula injury, per the Chargers’ injury report . Bold prediction: Young sacks Herbert twice. Blake Corum scores two touchdowns Blake Corum ran 17 times for 93 yards and a touchdown in Las Vegas, and he had two more scores, from 2 and 43 yards, wiped out by penalties, per the Rams . Kyren Williams’ third-quarter fumble opened the door for Corum , and Williams has lost two fumbles this season. Stafford likes what he has. “I haven’t had a tandem like this where they both can do everything,” he said on The Pat McAfee Show, per the Rams . Corum has 316 yards on 4.9 yards per carry. Bold prediction: Corum finds the end zone twice, and these ones count. Quentin Lake intercepts Herbert Quentin Lake wears the green dot now, and he’s earned it. He has two interceptions, and his eight pass breakups lead all safeties, according to PFF . His 79.1 coverage grade ranks seventh at the position. “Having the dot, it’s a privilege. It shows that the coaching staff they trust in you,” Lake said, per the team’s website . Herbert has thrown eight interceptions with 14 turnover-worthy plays, and his 44.5 PFF grade ranks last among 35 quarterbacks. Bold prediction: Lake picks off Herbert for his third interception. Puka Nacua tops 100 yards Davante Adams is out after cleanout surgery, with a 6-to-10-week timeline that McVay said is projected to land “on the shorter end,” per the Rams . That leaves more for Puka Nacua, who has 45 catches for 485 yards. His 90.0 grade ranks sixth among receivers, and he hasn’t dropped a pass, according to PFF . The Chargers’ secondary is banged up. Safety Derwin James missed both practices with a hamstring injury, and Jim Harbaugh said he could go on injured reserve, per the Chargers . Cornerback Donte Jackson was limited both days. We’ve asked whether Nacua’s body can hold up under this kind of workload, but Sunday sets up well for him. Bold prediction: Nacua goes over 100 yards for the first time since Adams went down. "I'm not sure yet. I'm not decided on those things." A follow-up question was asked with regard to when McVay would know whether or not either player would practice this week. McVay only offers further that he'll meet with the medical team and go from there. McVay doesn't offer any insight to how he thinks that meeting will go, just that he needs to meet with them before making a decision. "Once I get with Reggie and talk about the approach for the week. Then we'll just kinda follow their guidance based on where he's at and how he's feeling." It could be gamesmanship, it could be McVay wanted to have genuine deniability for this presser about whether Garrett will play this week or not, but at some point the team will need to make a decision on Garrett. And hopefully soon because the team invested a lot into him as an addition for a defense that is lacking serious firepower upfront this season. The Rams traded a first-round pick, Jared Verse, and more to to get Garrett . He hasn't played in a game since Week 1, as the 2025 sack leader has yet to notch one single sack or tackle for his new team. As McVay might say, "I'm not sure yet. I'm not decided on those things."

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 8 picks, including the Bills to top the Ravens in a high-scoring game Getty Images Going to the dogs last week turned out to be dog doodoo. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Pick: Seahawks 24, Bears 17 Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going. picks.blurb: Mile High Roundtable Drops its Predictions & Picks for Broncos-Chiefs Rematch Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Denver Broncos entered the 2026 with a few prime objectives, the first of which is winning the AFC West. The Broncos started on the wrong foot in that endeavor, getting blown out by the Kansas City Chiefs in the season opener on national television. However, seven weeks later, the Broncos have been through a gauntlet to open the season, and they've built up a sizable callus through seven weeks of brutal resistance training. Meanwhile, after starting the season 5-0, the Chiefs just suffered their first loss of the season to the Seattle Seahawks last week — a team the Broncos defeated the week prior. Now, the Chiefs head to Mile High to try to get back on the horse and avoid a two-game losing streak. The 5-2 Broncos have won three in a row, and after sweeping the Chiefs last year, they're looking to balance the scales this season . A win would give the Broncos the lead in the AFC West and put them on a path to repeating as division champs, especially given Kansas City's remaining schedule. How will this Broncos-Chiefs rematch shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Mile High Huddle / Denver Broncos On SI staff envisions this one unfolding at Mile High. Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 5-2 : After falling flat on their face against the Chiefs in Week 1, the Broncos' revenge mission is timely. Coming off a lopsided defeat against the Seahawks, the Chiefs run into a Broncos' offense that's finally showing signs of life, with quarterback Bo Nix getting loose. On Sunday, the Denver D stuffs the Chiefs' run game, and Nix finds Marvin Mims Jr. to put the game away late. Pick : Broncos 27, Chiefs 21 Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 5-2 : The Broncos haven't lost to the Chiefs at Mile High since Sean Payton became head coach. Nix is 2-0 at home against Kansas City, and with his confidence flooding back on the heels of his historic game last week, he takes another step forward in Week 8. With the exception of that Week 1 performance at Arrowhead, Nix usually saves his best play for the Chiefs. In this game, J.K. Dobbins turns in his best performance of the season, alongside Jonah Coleman, as the Broncos' offense galvanizes around its defense. A Wil Lutz field goal seals the win as time expires. Pick : Broncos 26, Chiefs 24 Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 5-2 : Last week's game was fairly easy to predict if you've watched this team long enough. For the same reason, however, this week's game is much less so. Will the Broncos avenge their Week 1 blowout or suffer a season sweep to their nemesis in Kansas City? Which squad will show up, the Good Broncos or the Bad Broncos? The angel on my shoulder says the former; the devil says the latter. But I've touched the proverbial hot stove and gotten burned enough over the years, so what's one more time? Pick : Broncos 20, Chiefs 19 Nick Kendell ( @NickKendellMHH ) 5-2 : It’s hard to predict what the Broncos will do this week with Zach Allen, Jaylen Waddle, and Talanoa Hufanga all injured . This game may come down to which team is healthier. However, I expect a redemptive effort by the Broncos' defense after the embarrassment Kenneth Walker III and the Chiefs put on them in Week 1. It was also against the Chiefs at Mile High when Nix turned the corner last season. Ultimately, it's an ugly one, but a win for Denver against the Chiefs, who lack pop offensively outside of Walker Pick : Broncos 20, Chiefs 17 Bob Morris ( @BobMorrisSports ) 5-2 : The Broncos were not good in Week 1 but have played better since. Meanwhile, the Chiefs are still a quality team but not a dominant one. I think the Broncos' defense has put its season-opening issues behind them, and the offense is showing improvement. Here's to hoping Nix plays with more confidence, Jonah Coleman makes an impact, and Marvin Mims Jr. steps up again, with the Broncos finding a way to win at home . Pick : Broncos 23, Chiefs 20 Bo Nix and Patrick Mahomes meet at midfield after a Broncos win at Mile High. | Dustin Bradford / IMAGO / Icon Sportswire Carl Dumler ( @CarlDumlerMHH ) 4-3 : I can't remember the last time a Week 8 game had so much on the line. The winner leads the division and has a very clear path to home-field advantage, in wildcard weekend, at least. Thankfully, this game is in Denver, and that home crowd will be alive and making life very difficult. The Broncos' defense will hold up its end, forcing a couple of turnovers, and making up for Week 1's lackluster showing. The Broncos' offense gets the run game going with Coleman back, and the play-action boot game finally yields some positive plays. The Broncos win a close one on a last-minute field goal. Pick : Broncos 24, Chiefs 21 Carl Dumler ( @CarlDumlerMHH ) 4-3 : I can't remember the last time a Week 8 game had so much on the line. The winner leads the division and has a very clear path to home-field advantage, in wildcard weekend, at least. Thankfully, this game is in Denver, and that home crowd will be alive and making life very difficult. The Broncos' defense will hold up its end, forcing a couple of turnovers, and making up for Week 1's lackluster showing. The Broncos' offense gets the run game going with Coleman back, and the play-action boot game finally yields some positive plays. The Broncos win a close one on a last-minute field goal. Pick : Broncos 24, Chiefs 21 Lance Sanderson ( @LanceS_MHH ) 4-3 : The Seahawks proved that if you stop Walker, you almost completely neuter the Chiefs' offense. The Chiefs don't have the skill-position players to make you pay on a consistent basis. Denver did a fairly good job of bottling up the Chiefs' run game at the line of scrimmage in Week 1, but couldn't get Walker to the ground due to poor tackling. That won't be the case this time around. Bolstered by arguably the best home-field advantage in the league, I fully expect a rambunctious defensive performance and the Broncos to be in first place in the AFC West on Sunday night. Pick : Broncos 23, Chiefs 16 James Campbell ( @JamesC_MHH ) 3-4 : If the Broncos want to repeat as division champs, this is the game to make it so. The Broncos have been playing better football of late, and Nix certainly looks healthier, but they have fundamental flaws, and the Chiefs are one of the teams best primed to expose them. Moving to Coleman is a welcome change and should provide a shot in the arm for the running game, but the performance of Travis Kelce and Walker against Denver's linebackers key a Chiefs win, as Kansas City finds a way to generate the explosive plays the Broncos do not. Pick : Chiefs 31, Broncos 14 Erick Trickel ( @ErickTrickel ) 3-4 : Nix bounced back against a terrible Arizona Cardinals defense, and the Chiefs are next. Kansas City's defense has struggled this season, so the opening is there for Nix to keep up his play. There's a chance to take the division lead in this one, but can the offense do enough, and can the defense tackle Walker and company? Denver wants to send a message that the first game was a fluke, with a 29.8% missed-tackle rate among other statistical outliers. However, Denver wins thanks to some big-time decisions from Sean Payton late, including going for a two-point conversion after a touchdown. Pick : Broncos 32, Chiefs 24 Dylan Von Arx ( @DylanVonArxMHH ) 3-4 : The Broncos handled the Cardinals but now must turn their attention to the Chiefs, who embarrassed them to open the season. The Broncos showed more life on offense last week, but Waddle's likely absence means Mims has to step up and contribute. The game being played in Denver may be the difference-maker, and I'm going with the Broncos to take the AFC West lead from the Chiefs' clutches. picks.headline: Week 8 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Chiefs look to bounce back vs. Broncos
picks.blurb: Week 8 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Chiefs look to bounce back vs. Broncos - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING NFL injury tracker live updates Ja out at least 4 weeks New head for D-Wade statue Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, October 29, 2026 at 3:49 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the Denver Broncos, Week 1 had to feel like a bad flashback. The first 12 times that Patrick Mahomes started against the Broncos, the Kansas City Chiefs won every time. Then there was a shift with Sean Payton in charge, and the Broncos won two of three against Mahomes and the Chiefs. The 2026 season opener, though, was like old times. It wasn't Mahomes that ruined the Broncos in the opener, though he played pretty well. It was Kenneth Walker III doing most of the damage, as he ran through many Denver missed tackles for 173 rushing yards. Also, the Chiefs' defense shut down Denver in a 31-10 win. It was a complete, impressive performance. It doesn't seem like much has changed since then. The Chiefs started 5-0 before losing last week at Seattle, a very tough opponent. The Broncos are 5-2 but questions persist about their offense. While the defense on the whole has been better for the Broncos, the run defense isn't great. Denver is 26th in EPA ( expected points added ) per rush allowed. It's easy to say that the Seahawks showed everyone how to beat the Chiefs — take Walker out of the game — but not everyone has Seattle's defense to pull that off. The Broncos showed once they aren't a great matchup against Walker. That's a big reason Kansas City -1.5 is the pick. We saw in the season opener that the Chiefs' dominance over the Broncos might not be over. Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III had 173 rushing yards in Week 1 against the Broncos. (AP Photo/Colin E. Braley) Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 8 of the NFL season: Panthers (+3.5) over Packers There's no way the Panthers are as bad as they played last week, when they were down 33-6 to the Buccaneers by halftime. Competent teams that get embarrassed usually bounce back well. The Packers are still a tough team to predict. Raiders (+1.5) over Jets The early East Coast start has been death for the Raiders for a long time, but they are probably the better team. They are certainly the better coached team. The Raiders are on a four-game losing streak but look at the opponents: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills, Rams. Those are four of the strongest teams in the NFL. If Las Vegas can't win here, it might be Fernando Mendoza time. Cowboys (-6.5) over Cardinals The Cowboys are going to score. The Cardinals have given up at least 30 points in six of their eight games. Dallas showed on Monday night that its offense is back, but what about the defense? Maybe a strong fourth quarter against the Eagles is a sign that the Cowboys' defense can be somewhat competent. It's scary to pick the Dallas laying points to anyone because they'll need to get stops, but it would be a surprise if they don't score 30. Buccaneers (-2.5) over Falcons Good luck figuring out either of these teams. The Buccaneers could be better than we think. Their only significant weakness has been pass offense, and that is explained by having an undrafted rookie starting three of their seven games. We don't know if Baker Mayfield is fully healthy, considering he had just 11 pass attempts in his return from a dislocated right thumb last week, but if he is maybe the Bucs can get on a roll. Browns (+3.5) over Steelers Teams coming back from an international game and playing right away without a bye are 0-3-1 this season. The losses were by 12, 11, and 6 points, and the close loss was by the Texans as a 10-point favorite last week. The tie was the Commanders when they were favored at home against the Giants. It's a hard turnaround, and it's what the Steelers face coming back from Paris last Sunday. Both of these teams are 5-2 but flawed, and I'll ride with the angle of the Browns not being the team that played in France last week. Jaguars (-9.5) over Colts It's hard to imagine being a Colts player this week. Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner were traded and everyone else with any value has to wonder if they're next. It's actually surprising the line is less than 10 points against a Jaguars team coming off a bye and a loss. This one could get really ugly. The remainder of the Colts' season could get really ugly. Ravens (+3.5) over Bills You've seen this here before: This all depends on if Lamar Jackson plays. This week, I assume he will. It seemed like he was close last week and he practiced in full on Wednesday. There would be some real frustration if he's not back for this game, which Baltimore might need to win to start to save its season. The Ravens' remaining schedule is the toughest in the NFL, according to DVOA . If he does play, we know the Bills defense is not very good. Getting more than a field goal seems good. Vikings (+3.5) over Lions If the Vikings' build was reversed, and they had a fun offense that was clearly one of the two best in the sport but a defense that was unreliable and among the 10 worst in the NFL, we'd respect them more. How do we know that? The 2026 Buffalo Bills, that's how. Minnesota's defense has been remarkable. Look at the Chicago Bears this season. In three of Caleb Williams' four starts, Chicago is averaging 39 points. In the other start, against the Vikings, the Bears scored three points at home (Williams got injured in that game but not until the middle of the fourth quarter). Maybe Detroit will figure out Brian Flores' defense, but nobody else has and I'm willing to take more than a field goal with the Vikings. Titans (+10.5) over Bengals The Titans have been blown out only twice. They lost by 13 to the Jets in Week 1 and 23 to the Texans in Week 5. Every other game has been decided by six or fewer points. The Titans have won only one of those games, but they're keeping it close. It's possible Joe Burrow will add to his growing MVP argument and torch Tennessee in a blowout, but this seems like a good spot for an ugly underdog. Rams (-6.5) over Chargers Typically, an 0-6 team coming off a bye would be a fine choice. The Chargers don't want to get embarrassed all season, but they're simply not a good team in any phase. That is shocking but also irrefutable. This is the exact type of contrarian pick I'd like to make but I just can't get there with the Chargers. Patriots (-7) over Dolphins It's possible the Dolphins get some confidence from their first win. It's also possible they let down a bit: It's still a 1-5 team whose goal was to get that first win out of the way. On the other side, there's a Patriots team coming off a loss with three extra days of rest. Commanders (-5.5) over Eagles A low point of this week was looking at the schedule and realizing this was the Sunday night game. Not fun. Not sure what's more surprising: That a 1-4-1 Commanders team is a 5.5-point favorite over the Eagles, or that the Commanders are the pick. The Eagles' best remaining effort was going to come on a Monday night against the rival Cowboys, and that effort was pretty meager. It won't get better. Bears (+3) over Seahawks The Sunday night game might not be good, but Monday night makes up for it. This one is fun (and should have been the Week 1 opener, but that's an old gripe). If there's an offensive coach that can figure out the Seahawks' defense, it's Ben Johnson. Caleb Williams has been on a heater since returning from a hamstring injury. Bet on the Chicago Bears to cover the spread on Monday night at sportsbooks On the other side, Seattle's offense will be happy to see the Bears defense after a tough stretch of opposing defenses, and perhaps Jaxon Smith-Njigba goes wild. It should be a good game, and if that holds true it'll be nice to have the underdog. Last week : 5-8-1 Season to date: 46-58-2

picks.headline: Chiefs vs. Broncos Preview: AFC West Rivals Prepare for Crucial Showdown
picks.blurb: Chiefs vs. Broncos Preview: AFC West Rivals Prepare for Crucial Showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING NFL injury tracker live updates Ja out at least 4 weeks New head for D-Wade statue Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Chiefs vs. Broncos Preview: AFC West Rivals Prepare for Crucial Showdown Photo by: Joe Camporeale Stephan Stroud Thu, October 29, 2026 at 8:28 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs will travel to Denver on Sunday for a crucial AFC West matchup against the Broncos. With Kansas City sitting at 5-1 and Denver at 5-2, both teams have plenty at stake as they look to strengthen their position in the division race. The game is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET at Empower Field at Mile High and will air on CBS. The Broncos enter with momentum after winning three consecutive games, while the Chiefs are looking to bounce back from their first loss of the season. Chiefs Look to Bounce Back Head coach Andy Reid and quarterback Patrick Mahomes will try to get Kansas City back on track after a disappointing 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. The Chiefs struggled to generate offense, finishing with just 213 total yards and failing to reach the red zone. Mahomes threw for 165 yards and an interception in the defeat. He will need a stronger performance against a Denver defense that has consistently pressured opposing quarterbacks this season. Running back Kenneth Walker III could be a major factor after dominating the Broncos in the teams' first meeting. Walker rushed for 173 yards and a touchdown in Kansas City's 31-10 victory in September. If the Chiefs can establish their ground game again, it could open opportunities for Mahomes and the passing attack. Broncos Aim to Protect Home Field Denver head coach Sean Payton will look to keep his team's winning streak alive behind quarterback Bo Nix. The second-year quarterback has shown his ability to make plays with both his arm and legs, and he delivered an impressive performance in the Broncos' 30-16 win over Arizona. Nix threw for 222 yards and added 73 rushing yards, including a 62 yard touchdown run. His mobility could be important against a Kansas City defense that will try to disrupt Denver's offensive rhythm. The Broncos' defense will also be key. Led by pass rushers Nik Bonitto and Zach Allen, Denver has the ability to pressure Mahomes and force mistakes. Cornerback Pat Surtain II's improved injury status could provide a boost to the secondary, although Denver's final injury report will be worth monitoring. What to Watch For The biggest matchup will be Kansas City's offense against Denver's pass rush. If the Broncos consistently pressure Mahomes, they could make life difficult for the Chiefs. However, Kansas City's experience and offensive talent make the visitors dangerous in any close game.

away.headline: What NFL draft experts saw in Omarr Norman-Lott before Chiefs selected him
away.blurb: The pick was not a popular one at the time, and a lot of people wondered why the Chiefs were drafting him so high when he likely would have been available on Day 3 of the draft. Clearly, Brett Veach saw something he liked in ONL and wanted him to be a member of the Chiefs' defense. The return to practice opens up a 21-day window during which the Chiefs can observe ONL and see how he's recovering. From there, they can either activate him to the active roster, or he'll remain on the PUP list for the rest of the season. The good news for Norman-Lott is that the Chiefs have options to rotate in and out on the defensive line, so he won't need to rush back. He's never been someone who has been on the field during the entire game, and that certainly won't change during his second season in the pros, especially one in which he's returning from a major injury. It's still good to be adding depth to this team at this point in the season. Norman-Lott was productive in college despite limited snaps, and the hope is that once Steve Spagnuolo finds an ideal role for him, he'll start to show that he was worthy of being a second-round pick. Remember Omarr Norman-Lott? The Kansas City Chiefs selected him in the second round of the 2025 NFL Draft, and he played just five games as a rookie before landing on IR with an ACL injury. It's understandable if Chiefs fans forgot about Norman-Lott, though. After all, he hasn't played in an NFL game since October of 2025, and we haven't heard much about him at all since his injury. Well, it was recently reported that Norman-Lott returned to practice, marking the first official step toward being activated and getting back on the field for Kansas City. Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star was the first to report that ONL was returning to practice . Omarr Norman-Lott's career to this point Norman-Lott played college ball at Arizona State for three years before transferring to Tennessee for the final two years of his eligibility. His sack numbers skyrocketed with the Volunteers, as he tallied 5.5 in 2023 and 4.0 in 2024, compared to the four total he had during his time with Arizona State. As for where he was projected to go in the draft, Lance Zierlein of NFL.com had him as either a third- or fourth-rounder. "Norman-Lott is an energetic pass rusher with a high pressure rate. He plays with harmonious hands and feet that work to and around edges, but he won’t offer much as a power rusher. His lack of size could hurt his draft slotting, but he has the potential to become a rotational defender and sub-package rusher." Dane Brugler of The Athletic also had ONL as a third- or fourth-rounder, citing that a full-time role could be difficult for him. "There is no doubt about his NFL talent, but his ability to handle more of a full-time role is a tricky projection."
