away.headline: Justin Tucker Returning To NFL, Joins Kansas City Chiefs
away.blurb: Justin Tucker Returning To NFL, Joins Kansas City Chiefs - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL TRENDING NFL injury tracker live updates Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Justin Tucker Returning To NFL, Joins Kansas City Chiefs Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Former All-Pro kicker Justin Tucker is returning to the NFL at the age of 36. Tucker is considered to be one of the greatest kickers in NFL history, which makes sense considering he's made 89.1% of his field goal attempts. His time with the Ravens ultimately came to an end after he was accused of inappropriate behavior during massage sessions. The Baltimore Banner reported that 16 massage therapists made accusations against Tucker, with two of the massage parlors claiming they banned him because of his behavior. "I did not act inappropriately at any point before, during, or after a professional bodywork treatment session, nor have I ever been told I am unwelcome at any massage therapy provider," Tucker told OutKick . "I absolutely respect the massage therapy profession and more so the individuals who work as massage therapists." Tucker has conducted workouts with the Colts, Jets and Saints over the past two years. It wasn't until this Wednesday, however, that he landed a deal. According to Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star, the Chiefs are signing Tucker to their practice squad. BALTIMORE, MARYLAND – DECEMBER 12: Kicker Justin Tucker #9 of the Baltimore Ravens talks to his wife, Amanda Bass, before playing against the New York Jets at M&T Bank Stadium on December 12, 2019 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images)Patrick Smith/Getty Images Harrison Butker has made plenty of big-time kicks for the Chiefs over the past decade, but he seems to be on the decline. Butker has made 11 of 16 field goal attempts this season. He had two crucial misses on Sunday night against the Seahawks. If Tucker outperforms Butker at practice, he could end up starting as early as this Sunday against the Broncos.

away.headline: Rashee Rice Returning in Week 8 for Kansas City Chiefs
away.blurb: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice will return from a hamstring injury Sunday against the Denver Broncos, head coach Andy Reid confirmed . Rice exited the Week 4 game with a hamstring injury in the first quarter and missed the last two games. Rice has 13 catches for 190 yards and a touchdown on the season. He had two catches for 19 yards and the lone touchdown against the Denver Broncos, who the Chiefs face in Week 8. In four career games against the Broncos, Rice has 16 catches for 185 yards and the lone touchdown. On the other side, the Broncos expect top cornerback Pat Surtain II to return after a three-game absence. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes has struggled to move the ball downfield without Rice, who serves as the No. 1 receiver. home.headline: Broncos' first injury report for Week 8 paints an early bleak picture
home.blurb: Of note, Patrick Surtain II pracitced in full, so the Broncos should get him back, but all of Allen, Waddle, and Talanoa Hufanga did not practice: The initial report with Waddle was that he aggravated his chest injury, but that there is 'hope' he can play on Sunday. Hufanga has already missed a couple of games due to his ankle injury, and if he does not practice in some capacity on Thursday, his status for Week 8 is in doubt. Allen has a hamstring injury and did not practice, either. The weird thing is that there was not any sort of report that came out with Allen's injury like we saw with Waddle, so that could end up being good news that it's pretty minor. We're definitely not going to make any declarations here since it's early in the week, but the Thursday statuses are going to be huge, as if any of the three "DNP" players from Wednesday are limited or full on Thursday, their chances of playing go way up. Sean Payton hilariously called himself out for awful Jaylen Waddle play call The Denver Broncos have consistently been among the healthiest teams in the NFL since Sean Payton took over back in 2023. That doesn't mean, though, the team has not dealt with injuries. Every NFL team has to deal with injuries in some capacity, and the teams that are usually standing in the end have better depth or better roster health overall. In Week 7, a win over the Arizona Cardinals, the Broncos saw two key players leave the game in wide receiver Jaylen Waddle, and defensive end Zach Allen. And in the team's first injury report of Week 8, we see some key players on the report, and while it is early, their statuses for Week 8 could already be in doubt. Denver Broncos injury report is getting longer as Week 8 approaches However, if any of them again do not practice on Thursday, it would logically be unlikely that they play on Sunday. While the Broncos are more talented than Kansas City and get this game at home, not having even one of these players is going to be brutal. In the same way that 2025's home game against the Chiefs was important, this one is as well. The Broncos would be in first place in the AFC West with a win, but if they lose, the Chiefs would improve to 6-1, and Denver would drop to 5-3 with two losses to the Chiefs already etched into their record. It would severely hurt their chances at repeating as division champions. And as it concerns the pasing game, if the Broncos hope to build on their breakout from Week 7, having Waddle in the lineup would allow that to continue to happen. picks.blurb: Patriots vs. Dolphins bold predictions for AFC East clash in NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING NFL injury tracker live updates Ja out at least 4 weeks New head for D-Wade statue Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Patriots vs. Dolphins bold predictions for AFC East clash in NFL Week 8 Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints Fri, October 30, 2026 at 5:29 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New England Patriots will be a rested and motivated team when they take the field in South Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins . The Patriots lost a hard-fought game against the Chicago Bears last Thursday night, but the defeat was a competitive effort that demonstrated they could play on the road against a team with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. The assignment this week doesn't compare. The Dolphins lack the kind of talent on either side of the ball to put up a 60-minute fight against QB Drake Maye and a motivated Patriots team. Miami earned its first victory of the season in their Week 7 game against the New York Jets, but they benefitted greatly from an inefficient and sloppy game from the Jets. Patriots feeling good about their consistent level of play It is unlikely that the Patriots will come at them in a similar manner. New England has played four consecutive solid games, and three of them were victories. When they took down the Buffalo Bills on the road in Week 4, it demonstrated that Mike Vrabel 's team was back on track and was ready to make a run at the AFC East title once again. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) They are 1.5 games behind the first-place Bills, so they have quite a lot of work to do to get there. However, they have more than enough focus and talent to get past the Dolphins on the road. As the Patriots prepare for this game , they are fairly confident that their offense is on the right track. Mike Vrabel would like to see his defense pick up its level of play and start to force more turnovers. If New England can assert itself on the defensive side and take the ball away from its opponents, they are going to put games away much earlier in the second half and avoid the tension that comes with a game that goes down to the wire. That's what should happen in this game. Maye will throw for 275 yards and 2 TDs against Dolphins The Patriots will not look at this game as one they will win by merely showing up. Throughout the years, playing the Dolphins on the road has often been a chore that has regularly been unpleasant for the visitors. Even in the prime years of Tom Brady's leadership, the Patriots have regularly been pushed hard by the Dolphins. The Patriots are 17-40 all-time in games played in Miami. Maye will not take the Dolphins lightly. He should be close to his best because he appears to have overcome the poor start he had in early season games in Seattle and Jacksonville. Maye has risen quite a bit in the ranks of NFL quarterbacks after his early struggles. He has completed 141 of 214 passes for 1,784 yards with 13 TDs and 8 interceptions. Maye's ability to get away from the pass rush is a big part of his game. He has run for 211 yards and 2 TDs, but the most important part of his athleticism is his ability to get away from the pass rush and get the ball to his receivers. It seems very unlikely that the Dolphins secondary is going to stop tight end Hunter Henry along with wideouts Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas. The big question revolves around A.J. Brown. He has been limited by injuries this season and has played just three game and has caught just 9 passes for 101 yards. He may or may not be ready to contribute to the Patriots' effort in this game because his knee appears to have flared up. However, the Patriots are expecting him to become their go-to receiver at one point this season. Malik Willis will throw for 150 yards, but toss two interceptions Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images Vrabel wants to see his defense step up quite a bit in the weeks to come. When the Patriots made their charge last season, Maye and the offense got a big assist from the defense as it stepped up by forcing takeaways. The Pats are going to attempt to do this by putting pressure on QB Malik Willis. The former Packer has tried to keep the Dolphins afloat, but the Dolphins have just one win this season. Willis has completed 87 of 151 passes for 1,057 yards with a 4-4 TD-interception ratio. He has also rushed for 223 yards and 3 TDs. Willis has been sacked 16 times this season, and linebacker Elijah Ponder of the Patriots will be after him. Ponder leads New England with 5.5 sacks and should get at least 1.5 in this game. Willis will be trying to get the ball to Malik Washington. He leads the Dolphins with 26 receptions for 289 yards but he has yet to find the end zone. Bold game prediction: Patriots 33, Dolphins 13 The Patriots have too much talent and they are focused on playing consistent, error-free football from this point forward. While many Patriots teams have had problems on the road against the Dolphins, this team will not. Look for Maye and RB Rhamondre Stevenson to get the Patriots off to a good start, and the defense will keep the Dolphins from mounting a charge. The Patriots will have control of this game prior to the end of the third quarter and New England will gain its fourth win in five games. away.headline: AJ Brown injury update, latest news on Patriots WR's status for game vs. Dolphins
away.blurb: New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown is questionable for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins after missing practice this week with a knee injury. Brown was listed as limited with ankle and knee injuries on the Patriots' Wednesday injury report and did not practice in Thursday's session. When asked Wednesday if he was still working on regaining his explosiveness after his return from IR, Brown said, "Sometimes I see it, and sometimes I'm pushing through." NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported the news on Thursday, noting the issue "flared up" and that his status for Sunday is "up in the air." Brown suffered an ankle injury in Week 1 that sidelined him for four games. He returned for the Patriots' last two contests but indicated he was playing through something in Week 7. Brown took more than 100 snaps in those games, which were played in a span of just five days. He was targeted 16 times and made six catches for 75 yards across the stretch. "I know, obviously, I'm working on something, but there's no excuses," Brown said. Patriots EVP of player personnel Eliot Wolf told Yahoo Sports' Jori Epstein after acquiring Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles in June the wide receiver had a " degenerative knee condition ." "It's a factor, but we examined him," Wolf told Epstein in June. "He's got a knee that has some wear and tear that we were aware of. Our training staff and medical staff signed off on it." Wolf noted at the time Brown had missed just one regular-season game to a knee issue. Brown also downplayed the issue when asked about his knee health this summer. The Patriots are already missing Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins after the wide receivers were placed on injured reserve with shoulder and calf injuries, respectively. Pop Douglas was serving as the Patriots' WR1 in front of Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III with Brown absent from Thursday's practice, per ESPN's Mike Reiss . The Patriots also have wide receivers Chandler Brayboy, Kyle Dixon, Cameron Dorner and Ryan Miller on the practice squad . Brown's potential absence could put more pressure on the Patriots to improve their rushing attack. Quarterback Drake Maye has gained almost as much ground (211 yards) as top running back Rhamondre Stevenson (285 yards) through seven games. Stevenson, who also ranks fifth on the Patriots in receiving yards, could step up in the long term. Brown's absence still raises concerns about his long-term future before the three-year, $96 million extension he signed with the Eagles in 2024 kicks in next season.

And I’m excited that he’s going to get his opportunity this week.” “Everything that JuJu’s done so far is he’s worked really hard, he’s been physical, he’s done everything he can to get back on the practice field,” Hafley said. “So if we feel that JuJu is able to play and he clears, then he’s gonna go out there and play.” The Miami Dolphins could be down another key offensive lineman when they face the New England Patriots in Week 8. “It is not looking very good for Sunday,” Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Friday. Proctor played every snap in Miami’s Week 7 victory over the New York Jets. He also spoke to the media Monday before entering concussion protocol. Despite their 1-5 start, the Dolphins have found success running the football, with Proctor playing a key role up front. Miami is averaging 131.5 rushing yards per game, seventh-best in the NFL. In six games this season, Proctor has allowed just one sack and committed three penalties. If he cannot play Sunday, Jarrett Kingston appears poised to step into the starting lineup. Kingston has played 13% of Miami’s offensive snaps and 16% of its special-teams snaps this season. He also saw meaningful playing time during the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals after right guard Jonah Savaiinaea suffered an ankle injury. Hafley expressed confidence in Kingston, who has been preparing to potentially switch sides along the offensive line. “We’ve seen it in practice and we have confidence in him,” Hafley said. “So switching sides, he’s looked at this week in practice and I’m sure he’s done both in his career, so I’m excited for him.” Hafley also emphasized that injuries create opportunities for other players to prove themselves and develop. There’s better news on the injury front for Miami’s secondary. Cornerback JuJu Brents, who is also in concussion protocol, practiced fully Friday. That marks another important step toward getting cleared for Sunday’s game. David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reported that Brents was no longer wearing a red, non-contact jersey Friday, indicating he had been cleared for contact. Hafley said Brents has done everything possible to get back on the field. The Dolphins could still be without a key piece of their offensive line, but getting Brents back would provide a much-needed boost to a defense preparing for a tough AFC East matchup. Now, Miami will have to wait and see whether Proctor can make a late push to join him on the field Sunday.

home.headline: AJ Brown injury update, latest news on Patriots WR's status for game vs. Dolphins
home.blurb: New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown is questionable for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins after missing practice this week with a knee injury. Brown was listed as limited with ankle and knee injuries on the Patriots' Wednesday injury report and did not practice in Thursday's session. When asked Wednesday if he was still working on regaining his explosiveness after his return from IR, Brown said, "Sometimes I see it, and sometimes I'm pushing through." NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported the news on Thursday, noting the issue "flared up" and that his status for Sunday is "up in the air." Brown suffered an ankle injury in Week 1 that sidelined him for four games. He returned for the Patriots' last two contests but indicated he was playing through something in Week 7. Brown took more than 100 snaps in those games, which were played in a span of just five days. He was targeted 16 times and made six catches for 75 yards across the stretch. "I know, obviously, I'm working on something, but there's no excuses," Brown said. Patriots EVP of player personnel Eliot Wolf told Yahoo Sports' Jori Epstein after acquiring Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles in June the wide receiver had a " degenerative knee condition ." "It's a factor, but we examined him," Wolf told Epstein in June. "He's got a knee that has some wear and tear that we were aware of. Our training staff and medical staff signed off on it." Wolf noted at the time Brown had missed just one regular-season game to a knee issue. Brown also downplayed the issue when asked about his knee health this summer. The Patriots are already missing Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins after the wide receivers were placed on injured reserve with shoulder and calf injuries, respectively. Pop Douglas was serving as the Patriots' WR1 in front of Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III with Brown absent from Thursday's practice, per ESPN's Mike Reiss . The Patriots also have wide receivers Chandler Brayboy, Kyle Dixon, Cameron Dorner and Ryan Miller on the practice squad . Brown's potential absence could put more pressure on the Patriots to improve their rushing attack. Quarterback Drake Maye has gained almost as much ground (211 yards) as top running back Rhamondre Stevenson (285 yards) through seven games. Stevenson, who also ranks fifth on the Patriots in receiving yards, could step up in the long term. Brown's absence still raises concerns about his long-term future before the three-year, $96 million extension he signed with the Eagles in 2024 kicks in next season.

home.headline: Patriots vs. Dolphins Friday injury report: A.J. Brown among New England’s questionable for Week 8
home.blurb: A.J. Brown headlines the team’s questionable to face the Miami Dolphins after going from a limited participant to missing consecutive practices to end AFC East prep. The three-time All-Pro wide receiver is dealing with a knee issue that flared up while also working back from the high ankle sprain that sent him to injured reserve in September. “His status is questionable, like some other players,” head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Friday. “We’ll see how he comes in tomorrow and we’ll make a decision.” Running back TreVeyon Henderson and linebacker Christian Elliss are also among New England’s questionable for Sunday’s 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff at Hard Rock Stadium. Brown has played 101 out of 122 offensive snaps since being activated midway through October. The June trade acquisition has caught six passes for 75 yards through those two starts. And with fellow veterans Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins both on injured reserve , the Patriots stand with three healthy wide receivers on the 53-man roster in DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams. “Just like everything else when you come out of the game or a long week, practice on Monday and evaluate the player. Just wasn’t able to finish practice on Wednesday,” Vrabel said. “So we continue to treat him and we’ll see where he is tomorrow.” “We’re really here focused on trying to get a win on the road in the division,” added Vrabel, “and we’ll make a decision on the guys that are questionable tomorrow.” The New England Patriots will wait for the weekend before making a final call on No. 1. Here’s the early game statuses. RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) In addition to Brown’s recent absences, Henderson was not spotted for back-to-back practices because of an illness. The sophomore running back has logged 203 rushing yards, 45 receiving yards and one touchdown through 57 touches this fall for an active depth chart also featuring Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner. As for Elliss, the off-ball linebacker has been a full participant for the past two weeks while managing a chest injury. He ranks atop the Patriots’ defense with 51 tackles through seven starts and has tacked on one sack, one forced fumble and a handful of quarterback hits.

Could A.J. Brown be a game-time decision for Dolphins game? picks.headline: 4 bold predictions in the Commanders' showdown with the Eagles, starting with Jayden Daniels
picks.blurb: Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders get their rematch with the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday night, and very little about it looks like the opener. Philadelphia won that one 24-22 when Washington’s tying two-point try was stuffed. Since then, Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for the season with blood clots in his lungs, and the Eagles have lost five straight, their longest skid since 2016. Washington (1-4-1) comes off its bye after a 23-17 loss in San Francisco that also cost it Terry McLaurin, who tore his patellar tendon and is done for the season, according to the team . Head coach Dan Quinn called the week off “a much-needed reset in a lot of ways,” per the team’s website . Philadelphia (2-5) lost 38-21 to Dallas on Monday night with Tanner McKee at quarterback. The Commanders are about a six-point favorite at Northwest Stadium and hold the EPA edge in nine of 12 categories. Here are four bold predictions for Sunday Night Football. Jayden Daniels leads Washington in rushing Daniels has 213 rushing yards on 25 carries, 8.5 per attempt, in four games, and his 88.7 rushing grade ranks third among quarterbacks, according to PFF . He has played the last two games in a brace after dislocating his left elbow in Week 2, and he ran only four times for 10 yards in San Francisco. He was a full participant in practice Wednesday and Thursday. Washington needs him to run. Jacory Croskey-Merritt is on injured reserve with a groin injury , leaving Rachaad White (36 carries, 145 yards) as the lead back. Philadelphia ranks 27th against the run at 131.4 yards per game, and Javonte Williams ran for 155 yards against the Eagles on Monday. Bold prediction: Daniels runs for 75 yards and a touchdown, more than any Washington running back. Washington sacks Tanner McKee four times Quinn’s defense blitzes more than any team except Minnesota, and it has only 11 sacks, tied for 22nd. “I’d love to see us, whether it’s blitzing or rush coverage together, really being in sync with that,” Quinn said Wednesday, per the team’s website . Odafe Oweh leads the team with three sacks on 15 pressures, according to PFF , though he hasn’t played up to his contract yet. K’Lavon Chaisson has 2.5 sacks and two forced fumbles. McKee is working behind a line that has allowed 18 sacks, and the Eagles had no sacks or quarterback hits of their own against Dallas. Bold prediction: Washington sacks McKee four times, even with Javon Kinlaw likely out with a knee injury. Antonio Williams beats Zack Baun this time Week 1 belonged to Zack Baun. Washington targeted him six times in coverage, and its pass catchers finished with minus-2 yards against him, per Next Gen Stats. He added 12 tackles and was named NFC Defensive Player of the Week . Baun is still fifth among linebackers with a 79.5 grade, but he has allowed a 100.0 passer rating in coverage, according to PFF . With McLaurin out, the rookie is the receiver Washington needs to change the equation . Antonio Williams has 18 catches for 205 yards and a touchdown, and he caught four passes for 64 yards and a score in the opener. Bold prediction: Williams goes over 75 yards, and at least one of those catches comes with Baun in coverage. Sonny Styles forces a turnover Sonny Styles leads Washington with 46 tackles and has an interception, a sack and a forced fumble. He made 13 tackles in San Francisco, per NBC Washington , and his 72.7 coverage grade ranks 10th among linebackers, according to PFF . Philadelphia’s offense ranks 29th in EPA, and Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks all missed practice Thursday, per the Eagles . That could leave McKee leaning on Dallas Goedert and Makai Lemon over the middle, where Styles does his work. Washington is plus-6 in turnover differential, second in the NFL . Bold prediction: Styles forces a fumble or picks off McKee. away.blurb: Dallas Goedert is good to go for Monday, while Saquon Barkley and Jalyx Hunt inch closer to a potential return. "It's just kind of the same injury that I sustained earlier. I just had a little bit of inflammation in there, had to let that settle down, but felt really good running out there today," Goedert said after Saturday's practice. "I want to be out there anytime I can. We only get 17 games. To miss a game, to miss two games, it always stinks. So if I can be available, I'm going to do everything I can to play. "I'm going to go out there and do whatever I can to help the team win, whether it's run blocking, pass blocking, or hopefully get a couple catches. home.blurb: Even in a limited role against the Cowboys, Barkley led the Eagles with 62 yards rushing on 7 carries. This after missing the previous two games with a hamstring injury. Barkley tweaked the hamstring on his first carry against Dallas, which went for 29 yards. Then he hurt his back by trying to overcompensate. At wide receiver, the four available are rookie Makai Lemon, Hollywood Brown, Darius Cooper and Elijah Moore. At linebacker, Jeremiah Trotter would take over for Campbell. The two had been splitting snaps the past two games. But the Eagles' top two wide receivers in DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were not practicing for a third straight day, a sign that each will miss their second straight game when the Eagles face the Washington Commanders on Nov. 1. In addition, linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) and punt returner Britain Covey (knee) weren't practicing for a third straight day. The Eagles are releasing their final injury and status report later on Oct. 30. Buy Philadelphia Eagles tickets After practice, Barkley said he "would hope so," when asked if he'll play against the Commanders. "I believe that I'll be able to." If Barkley can't play, the Eagles will be down to two running backs in Elijah Mitchell, who's still on the practice squad, and Jaydon Blue. They would be the sixth and seventh running backs to see action this season. Even if Barkley does play, he said he will likely be on a pitch count, and the Eagles will still need Mitchell and/or Blue. Either way, Barkley said even getting only 9 snaps, like he did against the Cowboys on Oct. 26, is better than not playing at all. When asked why, he replied: "There's one day I'm not going to be playing football. Whenever that is, I don't want to look back and be like, "I could've given it a chance and I didn't.' That's kind of what I live by. So I try my best to just keep recovering, being smart. But I like playing football. So if I have an opportunity to play, try my best to play." home.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles opened their Week 8 preparations Wednesday with an extensive injury report, listing six players as nonparticipants and another six as limited participants ahead of Sunday's NFC East matchup against the Washington Commanders . Barkley's status remains one of the biggest concerns after the veteran suffered a back injury during Monday night's 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. The Eagles listed him with hamstring and back injuries Wednesday, adding another concern for a player who recently returned from a hamstring issue that kept him out of consecutive games. Barkley opened the Dallas matchup with a 29-yard run and scored a touchdown on Philadelphia's first possession, but his workload was limited after his back tightened. He eventually left the game, forcing the Eagles to rely on their remaining running backs. Lemon responded with his first career touchdown reception against the Cowboys, but the Eagles would benefit from having additional receiving options available against Washington. Campbell was listed as a nonparticipant with hamstring and quadriceps injuries, adding to concerns for a defense that struggled against Dallas. Jones was sidelined by a hamstring injury, while Covey was listed with a knee injury after leaving Monday night's game. The defensive injury situation extends beyond those six players. Outside linebackers Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt and Nolan Smith were all listed as limited participants, along with defensive backs Michael Carter II, linebacker Smael Mondon Jr. and defensive tackle Moro Ojomo. The Eagles return to practice Thursday, and actual participation should better indicate which players are progressing toward Sunday's game. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sam Householder Thu, October 29, 2026 at 4:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Good teams play in big games and the Chicago Bears have a big game this week. They hit road to play the Super Bowl-champion Seattle Seahawks. And they'll do it with a brand new All-Pro defensive tackle! Jeffery Simmons is a Bear! The Bears are proving themselves to be one of the best offenses in the league with one of the best rising-star quarterbacks. And their head coach and quarterback face a huge test against one of the league's best defenses. Chicago didn't fare so well in their first defensive test of the year, against the Minnesota Vikings. However, the weather was a factor in that game, like it or not. Plus, Caleb Williams didn't finish the game. Excuses, maybe, but also realities. This matchup has a lot of great storylines and will be a measuring stick for the Bears to see how they compete against the league's best. It feels like a game with playoff implications. It feels like a game worthy of the Monday Night Football spotlight. It will be the first game in November for the Bears, too. When teams really start to separate themselves. Let's meet the Seahawks. Seattle Seahawks SB Nation site : Field Gulls Record: 4-3, second in the NFC West Last week: 20-3 win over the Kansas City Chiefs Game day, time, TV: Monday, 7:15 p.m. CT, ESPN Spread: Seattle -3.5 Bears all-time record against: 8-12, including 2-0 postseason Historical meeting: The Bears have never beaten the Seahawks in the month of November. In the second-ever meeting between the teams, the Seahawks beat the Bears 31-29 in week 10 of 1978. The Bears fell behind 21-9 with Jim Zorn hitting Steve Largent twice for touchdowns and Sherman Smith rushing for another. But Chicago made a strong comeback. Roland Harper scored on a 20-yard pass from Mike Phipps. After another Smith touchdown, Walter Payton scored from 7 yards out, drawing the Bears within six. The Seahawks drove down the field and tacked on another field goal to go up 31-22. Phipps threw a pick but Sam McCullum intercepted Zorn right back. Phipps put together a good drive and Harper scored a 2-yard TD with 40 seconds left. The Bears managed to recover the onside kick but with 12 seconds left, from Seattle's 46-yard line, Phipps' pass was intercepted to end the game. Last meeting: Who could forget the awful, terrible 6-3 Thursday Night Football game? Thomas Brown was coaching the Bears. It was a defensive slugfest. Or a total offensive mess. Depends on how you remember it. The most memorable play didn't count, as Caleb Williams rolled out and threw an off-platform pass to Rome Odunze four a touchdown. It was called back for offensive holding. (I cannot find a clip online, but I remember it was awesome). Offense: The Seahawks offense ranks 13th in points and 15th in yards. Their passing offense is 16th and their rushing offense ranks 17th. Sam Darnold (62.1 pct. cmp./1,290 yds./8 TD/8 INT) currently leads the league in interceptions, but played a lot better last week. Unless you've been living under a rock, you likely know about Jaxon Smith-Njigba (58 rec./867 yds./8 TD). Beyond him are AJ Barner (19/180/0), Cooper Kupp (18/199/1), deep threat Rashid Shaheed (16/163/0) and George Holani (12/88/0). Jadarian Price (28 att./119 yds./0 TD) is injured, but expected to return to practice this week along with Zach Charbonnett (no stats in 2026 yet). In their absence, it's been Emanuel Wilson (111 att./403 yds./3 TD) and Holani (26/108/1). Defense: Seattle's defense comes into Monday night as one the league's best. They rank fourth in points allowed and first in yards allowed. Their passing defense ranks first in passing yards and sixth in rushing. The loaded unit stars Nick Emmanwori (27 tkls/3 TFL/2 sk/1 PD/7 QB hits), DTs Leonard Williams (3 sk/7 TFL/9 QB hits/1 PD), Byron Murphy (3 sk/ 24 tkls/5 TFL/6 QB hits) Derick Hall (3 sk/19 QB hits/3 TFL/1 FF/1 FR) and Ernest Jones (3 sk/68 tkls/3 TFL/2 QB hits/1 INT/3 PD) and Devon Witherspoon (41 tkls/3 PD/3 TFL/1 QB hits) Other playmakers are Julian Love (2 INT/6 PD/24 tkls/2 TFL), Nehemiah Pritchett (13 tkls/4 PD/2 INT) and Josh Jobe (27 tkls/1 PD/1 INT/1 TFL). Key matchups: This is a top offense against a top defense. The Bears are going to have to play disciplined football. Take what their given, take shots when they can, use play-action to suck in the LBs. On defense, stop JSN. That's no easy task. The Seahawks can find a running game if Price and/or Charbonnett are back. Anyway to get pressure on Sam Darnold is good though; we know what happens when he is pressured. The Seahawks haven't allowed a 300-yard passer this season. The Rams are the only team with more than 300 passing yards against Seattle since week 2 of last season. Seattle has lost only three times at home going back to the beginning of last season. The 49ers are the only team to beat Seattle at home during this span Despite their strong numbers, the Seahawks have allowed opponents to score on 78.6 percent of their trips inside of the red zone. The Seahawks' 13 offensive turnovers on the season rank fourth-most in the league. Their 12 defensive turnovers rank third-most. Seattle is allowing a league-low 144.4 passing yards per game and the second-worst passer rating of 72.6. Only the Vikings allow a worse QB rating Can the Bears hang with a team as good as the Seahawks? How will their offense and QB measure up against Seattle's defense?

picks.headline: Bears vs. Seahawks bold predictions for Week 8 Monday Night Football
picks.blurb: Bears vs. Seahawks bold predictions for Week 8 Monday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING NFL injury tracker live updates Ja out at least 4 weeks New head for D-Wade statue Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Bears vs. Seahawks bold predictions for Week 8 Monday Night Football Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints Wed, October 28, 2026 at 11:24 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chicago Bears have demonstrated quite a bit of explosiveness this season, especially when Caleb Williams is under center and running back Kyle Monangai is healthy and in the lineup. Williams has been in the lineup for the past two games and has demonstrated no ill effects from the hamstring injury that sidelined him earlier in the year. Monangai has missed the last three games and while he is improving, there are no guarantees that he will be back in the lineup for this game. The Seahawks have not been at their best in the first half of the season and they take a 4-3 record into this home game. They are coming off a key Sunday night victory over the Kansas City Chiefs in which their defense performed at a peak level. They will need that kind of effort against the Bears. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Sam Darnold was one of the keys to Seattle's surge to last year's Super Bowl title. He has not been as efficient this season, as interceptions have been an issue. The Bears defense got a huge lift from their ability to create takeaways last year. They have not been as proficient in that area this season — minus-1 on the takeaway/turnover table — but they have been a middle-of-the-pack defense that has been moderately capable this season. This game could come down to turnover differential, and if the Bears are going to win on the road, they have to gain an advantage in this area. Williams will throw for 250 yards and 2 TDs Williams has demonstrated that he can rise to the occasion and handle pressure. He has an excellent partnership with head coach Ben Johnson, and it appears that those two will allow the Bears to remain contenders in the division and the NFC for several years. Williams has all the tools that an outstanding quarterback needs, and as the No. 1 selection in the 2024 NFL Draft, nearly all scouts and personnel specialists were predicting great things for him. However, Williams struggled in his rookie season under former head coach Matt Eberflus. That coach did not have the wherewithal to teach and demand outstanding play from Williams. However that changed under Johnson, and the quarterback reads and understands defenses, and he knows how to pick apart good defenses and make key plays. The one area that scouts did not get right about Williams was his speed and escapability from the pocket. He was thought to be above average or good in that area, and that assessment did not give him enough credit. He is sensational in that area. He has a strong partnership with wide receivers Rome Odunze and Luther Burden, as well as big-play tight end Colston Loveland. This trio should be able to cause problems for the Seattle defense, which is one of the strongest units in the league. Williams and the receivers will not overpower the Seahawks defense, but the quarterback will throw 2 TD passes and approach the 275-yard mark. Smith-Njigba is unstoppable, will exceed 125 yards and score a TD Mandatory Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images The Bears regularly have to contend with outstanding receivers like Justin Jefferson, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Christian Watson in the NFC North. However, Seattle wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is at another level. He is coming off a sensational game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Smith-Njigba was targeted 12 times by Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold and he caught 9 passes for 150 yards and 1 touchdown. The Chiefs knew he was the central point of the Seattle offensive game plan, yet defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo could not do anything to slow him down. Stopping him was out of the question. Chicago defensive coordinator Dennis Allen will face the same issue. Allen certainly knows what it is like to face outstanding wideouts in the NFC North, but Smith-Njigba may be too strong for the Bears defense. He has caught 58 passes for 867 yards and 8 TDs, and asking CBs Jaylon Johnson, Malik Muhammad and Kyler Gordon to prevent him from making big plays will be folly. The best way for the Bears to go about it would be pressuring Darnold and keep him from delivering accurate passes. The Bears have registered 19 sacks and Darnold has been trapped 14 times thus far. Allen's top priority will be to make sure his personnel gets in Darnold's face and prevents him from getting the ball to Smith-Njigba. That scenario is unlikely, but it is Chicago's best defensive hope. Bold game prediction: Seahawks 27, Bears 24 The Bears have the weapons to go into Seattle and give the defending champions a battle for 60 minutes. This is the kind of game that Johnson and Williams would like to use as a measuring stick. However, the Seahawks have already lost 3 games and they can't afford to lose any more. They will have a major challenge chasing down the 49ers in the NFC West, and dropping a home game to a solid team is not in their plans. The Seahawks played their best all-around game against the Chiefs in Week 7, and they will stay on track against the Bears. Seattle wins a close, well-played game against Williams and the Bears. Seattle will need contributions from its top playmakers and another sweltering performance from its defense to give the team its best shot to secure a statement victory against Chicago. Here are three bold predictions for the primetime showdown slated for this coming Monday night. Seahawks will limit Caleb Williams to his worst performance of the season Bears quarterback Caleb Williams enters the matchup with 1,020 passing yards, five touchdowns and one interception, completing 71.0% of his passes this season. However, Seattle's defense will make life difficult for Williams, limiting his opportunities down the field and taking away his ability to be as dynamic as usual when scrambling out of the pocket. Williams will finish with season lows in completion percentage, passing yards and passing touchdowns thanks to Seattle's unit disrupting his rhythm. AJ Barner posts season-high receiving numbers AJ Barner has totaled 180 receiving yards on 19 catches this season but has yet to find the end zone through the air. Against the Bears, the Seahawks tight end will break out with season highs in receiving yards and touchdowns. His current season-high in receiving yards is 69 from Week 3. Seattle will be aggressive in attacking underneath and using Barner as a reliable target in key situations. Barner will ultimately record over 70 receiving yards and a receiving touchdown in the game. Seahawks reserve makes a big difference in win Seattle's depth will become a major factor as the game unfolds. Tyrice Knight will provide an important spark for the Seahawks with timely defensive stops, physical play and special-teams contributions. Knight himself will go for a sack, quarterback hit and tackle for loss in what will be his biggest game of the year. His impact will swing momentum in Seattle's favor and help the Seahawks take Williams out of his comfort zone and ultimately come away with a win in a hard-fought contest. away.headline: Seahawks' dark side defense facing injuries at bad time before Bears
away.blurb: ​Another factor is Thomas potentially returning to the Seahawks after missing two games. The player that replaced him, Knight, is also seeing some injury concerns. He has played great stepping in as a starter, but his availability is a concern. His backups in Chazz Surratt (calf), Patrick O’Connell (toe) and Connor O’Toole (hamstring) also become a concern after being limited in Thursday’s practice. ​Seattle is coming off a game where they held the league’s best rusher in Kansas City’s Kenneth Walker III to 36 yards on 14 carries. The Seahawks faced a limited Chiefs’ offense in Week 7, but the Bears are a lot more explosive with their passing game, with quarterback Caleb Williams, wide receiver Luther Burder and Rome Odunze. The Seahawks have opposing offenses to short-yardage situations, but they’ll have to take away the deep passing game the most. Through seven weeks into the 2026 NFL Season, the Seattle Seahawks (4-3 ) have one of the best, if not the best, defenses in the NFL. The Dark Side Defense has been the reason why the team remains one of the best teams competing for a Super Bowl title . Among the key reasons for their elite potential are their dynamic star players and a roster full of productive playmakers. ​Even the great defenses have some limits. The Seahawks’ defense has some injury concerns that could play a factor on Monday Night Football against the Chicago Bears (5-2). The Bears will be one of the most talented offenses the Seahawks will face this season. There isn’t a question of whether the Seahawks can beat the Bears, but are they healthy enough? ​Seahawks’ Defensive Injury Concerns ​Just a few days after humiliating the Kansas City Chiefs , the Dark Side Defense has some concerns with injuries. The Dark Side Defense has seven players with legitimate concerns on Thursday’s injury report. Among the biggest are defensive tackle Leonard Williams (Achilles), Tyrice Knight (hip), edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) and linebacker Drake Thomas (ankle). ​Nwosu didn’t participate in Thursday’s practice , leaving him with some serious doubt about not playing Monday night against the Bears. He is one of the more consistent pass rushers along the edge for the Dark Side Defense. Another consistent pass rusher for the Seahawks is Williams from the interior. He has a potentially scary injury that could be tough for him to play through, even if he feels great. ​Why the Bears are a Serious Threat ​The Bears aren’t the most productive offense they’ll face up to this point in the season. Chicago, however, has scored the sixth-most points in the league, averaging 25.7 points per game. The Bears are also second in the league in total yards per game (393.3). One of the big reasons is their rushing offense being first in rushing yards with 1,080. away.headline: Seahawks-Bears Thursday injury report: Cross and Shaheed out, ‘Big Cat’ limited with Achilles
away.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks have a lengthy injury report to start their prep for the showdown with the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football with a whopping 18(!!) players listed with some sort of designation. The DNP’s for injury included Charles Cross, Rashid Shaheed, and Uchenna Nwosu. Notable limited participants were Tyrice Knight, Drake Thomas, the newly-returning Jadarian Price, and Leonard Williams who popped up with an Achilles injury…maybe I shouldn’t have used the word “popped” in his case. Find some wood to knock on if you’re superstitious. As this is the first injury report of the week, we’ll need to see how things shake out over the next few days to see who is really in danger of missing the primetime game. New Seahawks Quenton Nelson was listed as a full participant along with Zach Charbonnet. The hope is that both of them along with potentially Jadarian Price will help take the run game to another level, thus lessening the load on Sam Darnold’s shoulders. Mike Macdonald seemed relatively positive about Cross, saying that IR wasn’t in consideration at this time. The less time he misses, the more he’ll get to gel with his new partner in crime on the left side in Nelson.

away.headline: Why Super Bowl Ambition, Not Injury Panic, Sparked Pre-Game Trades for Bears and Seahawks
away.blurb: The Chicago Bears and Seattle Seahawks sit at the edge of the NFC postseason picture, with the Seahawks on the bubble right now at 4-3. Both teams made major moves ahead of a massive Monday Night Football matchup in Week 8. Chicago swung for the fences with an unexpected trade for Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. The Bears sent the Titans a 2027 first-round draft pick, 2028 first-round draft pick, and 2027 fourth-round draft pick, receiving a 2028 fifth-round draft pick along with Simmons. Meanwhile, Seattle acquired guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts. The Seahawks sent the Colts a 2027 third-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round draft pick for the 30-year-old All-Pro guard. Chicago is thin on the defensive line due to injuries and the like, but there's been recent absences on the edge, not the middle. Seattle will be missing left tackle Charles Cross due to a high ankle sprain against the Bears, but the Seahawks didn't land Nelson to account for Anthony Bradford's injury woes this season at guard. Nelson is on a different level than anyone on Seattle's interior offensive line. It's clear the Seahawks feel they have a chance to repeat despite some Super Bowl hangover losses to the Washington Commanders and Denver Broncos. There may also now be a fix for one of the league's least effective run games early on. Jeffery Simmons, Quenton Nelson Face Off in Debuts For New Teams Many eyes will be on Simmons and Nelson this coming Monday, particularly because it'll be easy to track how each is doing when lined up against each other. Nelson will get the chance to open up gaps for Emanuel Wilson, who's become Seattle's top running back during an injury-stricken season for the room, as well as the returning Zach Charbonnet. Simmons will get the chance to prevent and plug those gaps in his Chicago debut. There were already plenty of subplots to be excited about on Monday. The Ryan Poles-John Schneider chess match with their trade deadline splashes taking center stage gives the Manningcast some great X's and O's fodder. It's either that or the tense Joe Buck-Troy Aikman booth. Unfortunately, America seems to love choosing the dysfunction over the practical, hence reality television still being consumed decades past its expiration date. Contenders make the right moves during the season, just as much as before it. Both the Seahawks and Bears front offices are letting their fans know that they are taking these next few months seriously. This is a bellwether game for these two teams. We'll see which franchise better accommodates its midseason splash and moves closer to the top of the NFC. away.headline: Week 8 Injury Report: Bears at Seahawks
away.blurb: Ten players were listed as limited, though in the case of veteran outside linebacker DeMarcus Lawrence, it was for rest. Among those limited were running back Jadarian Price (chest) who returned to practice from injured reserve this week, and linebackers Drake Thomas (ankle) and Chazz Surratt (calf), who have both missed multiple games with injuries. New to the injury report this week is defensive tackle Leonard Williams , who was limited with an Achilles injury. The Bears did not practice Thursday, so their report is an estimation, but running back Kyle Monangai was listed as a non-participant due to thumb and toe injuries, while linebacker D'Marco Jackson (ankle) and cornerback Malik Muhammad (toe) were listed as limited. news Ty Okada Out, Nick Emmanwori Questionable For Seahawks' Season Opener vs. Patriots Week 8 Injury Report: Bears at Seahawks Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS Presented by Week 8 Injury Report: Bears at Seahawks Details on the Seahawks’ injury situation heading into their Week 8 game vs. the Bears. home.headline: Seahawks' dark side defense facing injuries at bad time before Bears
home.blurb: ​Another factor is Thomas potentially returning to the Seahawks after missing two games. The player that replaced him, Knight, is also seeing some injury concerns. He has played great stepping in as a starter, but his availability is a concern. His backups in Chazz Surratt (calf), Patrick O’Connell (toe) and Connor O’Toole (hamstring) also become a concern after being limited in Thursday’s practice. ​Seattle is coming off a game where they held the league’s best rusher in Kansas City’s Kenneth Walker III to 36 yards on 14 carries. The Seahawks faced a limited Chiefs’ offense in Week 7, but the Bears are a lot more explosive with their passing game, with quarterback Caleb Williams, wide receiver Luther Burder and Rome Odunze. The Seahawks have opposing offenses to short-yardage situations, but they’ll have to take away the deep passing game the most. Through seven weeks into the 2026 NFL Season, the Seattle Seahawks (4-3 ) have one of the best, if not the best, defenses in the NFL. The Dark Side Defense has been the reason why the team remains one of the best teams competing for a Super Bowl title . Among the key reasons for their elite potential are their dynamic star players and a roster full of productive playmakers. ​Even the great defenses have some limits. The Seahawks’ defense has some injury concerns that could play a factor on Monday Night Football against the Chicago Bears (5-2). The Bears will be one of the most talented offenses the Seahawks will face this season. There isn’t a question of whether the Seahawks can beat the Bears, but are they healthy enough? ​Seahawks’ Defensive Injury Concerns ​Just a few days after humiliating the Kansas City Chiefs , the Dark Side Defense has some concerns with injuries. The Dark Side Defense has seven players with legitimate concerns on Thursday’s injury report. Among the biggest are defensive tackle Leonard Williams (Achilles), Tyrice Knight (hip), edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) and linebacker Drake Thomas (ankle). ​Nwosu didn’t participate in Thursday’s practice , leaving him with some serious doubt about not playing Monday night against the Bears. He is one of the more consistent pass rushers along the edge for the Dark Side Defense. Another consistent pass rusher for the Seahawks is Williams from the interior. He has a potentially scary injury that could be tough for him to play through, even if he feels great. ​Why the Bears are a Serious Threat ​The Bears aren’t the most productive offense they’ll face up to this point in the season. Chicago, however, has scored the sixth-most points in the league, averaging 25.7 points per game. The Bears are also second in the league in total yards per game (393.3). One of the big reasons is their rushing offense being first in rushing yards with 1,080. home.headline: Seahawks-Bears Thursday injury report: Cross and Shaheed out, ‘Big Cat’ limited with Achilles
home.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks have a lengthy injury report to start their prep for the showdown with the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football with a whopping 18(!!) players listed with some sort of designation. The DNP’s for injury included Charles Cross, Rashid Shaheed, and Uchenna Nwosu. Notable limited participants were Tyrice Knight, Drake Thomas, the newly-returning Jadarian Price, and Leonard Williams who popped up with an Achilles injury…maybe I shouldn’t have used the word “popped” in his case. Find some wood to knock on if you’re superstitious. As this is the first injury report of the week, we’ll need to see how things shake out over the next few days to see who is really in danger of missing the primetime game. New Seahawks Quenton Nelson was listed as a full participant along with Zach Charbonnet. The hope is that both of them along with potentially Jadarian Price will help take the run game to another level, thus lessening the load on Sam Darnold’s shoulders. Mike Macdonald seemed relatively positive about Cross, saying that IR wasn’t in consideration at this time. The less time he misses, the more he’ll get to gel with his new partner in crime on the left side in Nelson.
